items.name: Add BitLocker Recovery Password
items.description: Adds a RecoveryPassword protector to an already-encrypted OS volume that does not have one. Non-destructive and idempotent - it never removes an existing protector and never touches encryption state.

items.name: Backup BitLocker Key To Entra
items.description: Escrows every recovery password protector on the OS volume to Entra ID. Exits 10 on devices that are not Entra joined, where the call has nowhere to go.

items.name: Clear BITS Transfer Queue
items.description: Cancels BITS jobs older than seven days. A queue full of stalled jobs is what stops Windows Update, Defender and the Hub downloading anything, and it survives a restart.

items.name: Clear Browser Caches
items.description: Closes Edge and Chrome and clears their cache directories for the signed-in user. Cookies, passwords and profiles are left in place, so the user stays signed in - this only removes the cached content that causes a stale or broken page.

items.name: Clear Crash Dumps
items.description: Removes MEMORY.DMP and minidumps older than 30 days. The full dump is often several gigabytes; recent minidumps are kept because they are the evidence for a bugcheck that is still being investigated.

items.name: Clear Delivery Optimization Cache
items.description: Empties the Delivery Optimization peer cache, which can hold tens of gigabytes on a device that has been seeding for the office. Uses the built-in cmdlet where it exists and falls back to clearing the folder with the service stopped.

items.name: Clear Error Reporting Queue
items.description: Empties the Windows Error Reporting report queue and archive. On a device with a crashing application these folders quietly collect thousands of report directories and a surprising amount of disk.

items.name: Clear Expired Machine Certificates
items.description: Removes expired certificates from the LocalMachine personal store, leaving valid ones and every other store alone. Each removed thumbprint and subject is written to the log first, which is the only way back.

items.name: Clear Font Cache
items.description: Stops the font cache services, deletes the cache databases and starts them again. The fix for garbled or missing text in Office and Explorer after a font package deploys badly.

items.name: Clear Icon And Thumbnail Cache
items.description: Deletes the per-user icon and thumbnail cache databases for every profile that is not currently loaded, which fixes blank or wrong icons in Explorer. Skips loaded profiles because the files are locked while a user is signed in.

items.name: Clear Microsoft Teams Cache
items.description: Closes Teams and removes its cached web content for the signed-in user. Fixes a stuck sign-in, a blank client and stale presence without touching chat history, which lives in the service.

items.name: Clear Print Spooler Queue
items.description: Stops the spooler, deletes every queued job in the PRINTERS folder and starts the service again. Clears jobs stuck in a deleting or error state.

items.name: Clear Servicing Logs
items.description: Truncates the CBS and DISM log folders, which grow without bound on a device that has been failing updates for months. Keeps the newest log of each so a current failure is still diagnosable.

items.name: Clear User Temporary Files
items.description: Removes files older than seven days from the signed-in user's temp folder and the Internet Explorer cache. Runs in the user context so it reaches the profile a SYSTEM script cannot see, and never touches a file in use.

items.name: Clear Windows Temp
items.description: Deletes files in the machine temp folder that have not been touched in two days, so anything an installer is currently using is left alone. Reports megabytes reclaimed.

items.name: Clear Windows Update Cache
items.description: Stops the update services, empties the SoftwareDistribution download folder and starts them again. Narrower than a full component reset - it reclaims the space and clears a poisoned download without touching the datastore.

items.name: Collect Hub Diagnostic Logs
items.description: Copies the Hub, MDM diagnostic and provisioning logs into a single timestamped zip under ProgramData so a technician can collect one file instead of hunting five folders. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is deleted.

items.name: Disable Autologon
items.description: Clears AutoAdminLogon and removes the stored DefaultPassword value, which imaging tools frequently leave in the registry as clear text. The username is logged before removal so the leftover can be traced.

items.name: Disable AutoPlay And AutoRun
items.description: Sets NoDriveTypeAutoRun to 0xFF machine-wide and disables the AutoRun handler, closing the removable-media execution path. Applies at machine scope so it holds for every profile including new ones.

items.name: Disable Built-in Administrator
items.description: Disables the RID 500 account, matched by SID so a renamed account is still found. Exits 10 rather than acting when it is the only enabled local administrator, which would lock the device out.

items.name: Disable Consumer Experience Features
items.description: Turns off the Windows spotlight, suggested content and silently installed consumer apps at machine scope. Stops a corporate build re-acquiring games and promoted apps after every feature update.

items.name: Disable Fast Startup
items.description: Clears HiberbootEnabled so a shutdown is a real shutdown. Devices with fast startup on can go months without a genuine boot, which is why patches, drivers and startup scripts appear not to apply.

items.name: Disable Guest Account
items.description: Disables the RID 501 Guest account. Trivially safe and idempotent, and it closes a finding that appears in almost every baseline audit.

items.name: Disable Hibernation
items.description: Turns hibernation off and removes hiberfil.sys, which is worth several gigabytes on a small system drive. This also disables fast startup, which is usually the point on a managed fleet.

items.name: Disable IPv6 Transition Tunnels
items.description: Disables Teredo, 6to4 and ISATAP. These tunnels can carry traffic around an IPv4-only firewall policy and are almost never wanted on a managed endpoint. Native IPv6 on the adapter is left alone.

items.name: Disable Legacy TLS And SSL Protocols
items.description: Disables SSL 2.0, SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 for both client and server in SCHANNEL and leaves TLS 1.2 explicitly enabled. Takes effect on restart. Check line-of-business agents that still pin TLS 1.0 before deploying broadly.

items.name: Disable LLMNR And NetBIOS
items.description: Sets EnableMulticast to 0 and switches every interface's NetBIOS over TCP/IP to disabled, closing the two name-resolution paths responder tooling relies on. Prior NetBIOS values are logged per interface.

items.name: Disable Network Adapter Power Saving
items.description: Clears 'allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' on every physical network adapter. Stops the intermittent disconnects and slow wake-from-sleep that get blamed on the wireless network.

items.name: Disable Remote Assistance
items.description: Clears the Remote Assistance invitation and shadow settings and disables its firewall group, closing an inbound path that most managed fleets never use.

items.name: Disable Remote Desktop
items.description: Blocks inbound Remote Desktop by setting fDenyTSConnections and disabling the Remote Desktop firewall rule group. Intended for endpoint fleets where RDP is never the support path.

items.name: Disable SMBv1 Client
items.description: Sets the mrxsmb10 driver to disabled and clears its LanmanWorkstation dependency so the device can no longer speak SMBv1. The previous start value is written to the log before the change.

items.name: Disable USB Selective Suspend
items.description: Turns off USB selective suspend on the active power plan for both AC and battery. The usual cure for a dock that drops its network adapter or a headset that disconnects a few minutes into a call.

items.name: Disable WinRM Service
items.description: Stops the Windows Remote Management service, sets it to Disabled and removes its listeners. For fleets managed entirely through the Hub, where WinRM is attack surface rather than a management path.

items.name: Empty Recycle Bin
items.description: Empties every user's recycle bin on every fixed drive. This permanently deletes user data that a person may still be intending to restore - offer it in the catalog rather than assigning it silently.

items.name: Enable ASR Rules In Block Mode
items.description: Puts a conservative set of five Attack Surface Reduction rules into Block mode. Only the rules named here are touched, so audit-mode pilots of other rules are left exactly as they were.

items.name: Enable BitLocker On OS Drive
items.description: Encrypts the OS volume with XTS-AES 256 using the TPM plus a recovery password, used-space-only. Exits 10 when the TPM is not ready rather than starting an encryption that will fail. Pilot this before fleet assignment - it is the most consequential script in the library.

items.name: Enable Command Line Process Auditing
items.description: Turns on process creation auditing and includes the command line in event 4688. Without the command line the event names the binary but not what it was told to do, which is the part an investigation actually needs.

items.name: Enable Credential Guard
items.description: Configures VBS and Credential Guard with UEFI lock via the DeviceGuard policy keys. Exits 10 where the hardware cannot support it, and reports a pending restart rather than rebooting.

items.name: Enable Defender Cloud Protection
items.description: Sets cloud-delivered protection to Advanced and enables sample submission for safe samples. Reverts the two settings most often turned off during a troubleshooting session and never turned back on.

items.name: Enable Defender Network Protection
items.description: Puts network protection into block mode so outbound connections to known-bad hosts are stopped at the endpoint rather than only at the corporate egress. Audit mode is the safer first step if the fleet has not run it before.

items.name: Enable Defender Real-Time Protection
items.description: Turns Microsoft Defender real-time protection back on where it was disabled locally. Exits 10 when a third-party antivirus owns the endpoint, because Defender is passive by design there and forcing it would be wrong.

items.name: Enable Firewall All Profiles
items.description: Enables the Windows Firewall on any profile that is switched off and sets the inbound default to Block. Names the profiles it changed in the log so you can tell a local override from a policy failure.

items.name: Enable LSA Protection
items.description: Sets RunAsPPL so LSASS starts as a protected process. Takes effect at the next restart, so the script reports a pending reboot rather than forcing one.

items.name: Enable Memory Integrity
items.description: Turns on hypervisor-protected code integrity. Refuses to act when Windows reports an incompatible driver, because forcing it there produces a device that boots without HVCI and looks compliant in the registry.

items.name: Enable OneDrive Known Folder Move
items.description: Sets the silent account configuration and known folder move policies for the tenant id in esr_tenant_id, so Desktop, Documents and Pictures redirect into OneDrive without prompting the user. Applies at the next sign-in.

items.name: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging
items.description: Turns on script block logging and transcription to a local folder, so a malicious or simply mysterious script leaves a record in the PowerShell operational log. Pair it with a log size increase or the evidence rolls away.

items.name: Enable Storage Sense
items.description: Turns Storage Sense on machine-wide and sets it to run monthly, clearing temporary files and emptying the recycle bin after 30 days. Prevention rather than a one-off clean.

items.name: Enable Strong Crypto For .NET Framework
items.description: Sets SchUseStrongCrypto and SystemDefaultTlsVersions for the 32-bit and 64-bit .NET Framework 4 runtimes so managed applications negotiate TLS 1.2 instead of falling back. Pairs with disabling the legacy protocols.

items.name: Enable Windows Firewall Logging
items.description: Turns on dropped and allowed packet logging for all three firewall profiles and raises the log cap to 16 MB, so a blocked-connection complaint can be answered from pfirewall.log instead of guesswork.

items.name: Flush DNS Cache And Re-register Records
items.description: Clears the resolver cache, restarts the DNS Client service and re-registers the device's A records. First move for a device resolving a stale address after a site move or a DNS change.

items.name: Force Policy and MDM Sync
items.description: Runs a forced gpupdate, kicks the EnterpriseMgmt MDM sync scheduled tasks and restarts the Workspace ONE Hub service so the device checks in immediately.

items.name: Purge Kerberos Ticket Cache
items.description: Purges the machine and current-user Kerberos tickets so the next request gets a fresh ticket. Clears the access-denied on a file share that survives a group change, without waiting for a sign-out.

items.name: Re-enable Critical Scheduled Tasks
items.description: Re-enables the maintenance, defragmentation, restore point and telemetry-independent servicing tasks that optimiser tools disable. These are the tasks whose absence shows up months later as a device that never trims its SSD or cleans its component store.

items.name: Re-enable MDM Scheduled Tasks
items.description: Re-enables any disabled task under the EnterpriseMgmt folder and runs the schedule task once. A device that has stopped reporting compliance is very often a device whose MDM sync tasks were disabled by a cleanup tool.

items.name: Re-register Store Apps
items.description: Re-registers the inbox Store app packages for the currently signed-in user, which repairs a broken Start menu, Settings or Photos. Runs in user context because AppX registration is per user and a SYSTEM run registers nothing anyone will see.

items.name: Reclaim Disk Space
items.description: Purges system and per-user temp folders, the Windows Update download cache, CBS logs, the Delivery Optimization cache and the recycle bin, then reports how much space was recovered.

items.name: Remove Broken Provisioned App Packages
items.description: Finds provisioned app packages whose install folder is missing and removes the stale registration. These are the packages that make a feature update fail with an 0x80073712-family error and are invisible in Settings.

items.name: Remove Machine Proxy Configuration
items.description: Resets the WinHTTP proxy to direct access and removes a machine-wide Internet Settings proxy policy. Use when a decommissioned proxy is breaking Hub check-in or Windows Update. Per-user browser proxies are not touched - those live in each user's hive.

items.name: Remove PowerShell v2 Engine
items.description: Removes the PowerShell 2.0 optional feature, which bypasses AMSI and script block logging. Uses DISM through the optional-feature cmdlets and never reboots; the feature is gone at the next restart.

items.name: Remove Preinstalled Consumer Apps
items.description: Removes the comma-separated AppX packages listed in ESR_APPS for all users and from the provisioning store so they do not return for new profiles.

items.name: Remove Stale User Profiles
items.description: Deletes local profiles not used in 90 days, skipping loaded, special and administrator profiles. Uses the Win32_UserProfile Delete method so the registry ProfileList entry goes with the folder - deleting the folder alone is what creates a TEMP profile on next logon.

items.name: Remove Stale Wireless Profiles
items.description: Deletes all-user wireless profiles that are not on the keep list, so a device stops preferring a guest or hotel SSID over the corporate one. Set esr_wifi_keep to a comma-separated list of SSIDs to retain; anything not listed is removed.

items.name: Remove Unauthorized Local Admins
items.description: Removes members of the local Administrators group that are not on an allow list. Expects a UEM variable esr_admin_allowlist holding a semicolon-separated list of names or SIDs; with no variable set it logs what it would remove and exits 10 rather than guessing.

items.name: Remove Windows.old
items.description: Deletes the Windows.old folder left by a feature update, taking ownership of the tree first because its ACLs otherwise refuse SYSTEM. Removing it gives up the ability to roll the feature update back, so only run it past the ten-day window.

items.name: Remove WSUS Policy
items.description: Removes the WUServer and UseWUServer policy values that keep a device pointed at a decommissioned WSUS, then restarts the update service so the change takes effect. Only touches devices that actually carry the policy.

items.name: Renew DHCP Lease
items.description: Renews the lease on every DHCP-enabled adapter that currently holds an address, using the WMI renew method rather than a release-and-renew so a remote session is not dropped. Adapters with a static address are skipped.

items.name: Repair Windows Time Synchronisation
items.description: Restarts the Windows Time service and forces a resync; if that fails it unregisters and re-registers w32time and tries again. Fixes the Kerberos and certificate failures a drifted clock causes.

items.name: Require Network Level Authentication For RDP
items.description: Turns on Network Level Authentication for Remote Desktop so a session is authenticated before a desktop is created. Leave RDP itself as it is - this only hardens it where it is deliberately in use.

items.name: Require SMB Signing
items.description: Turns on required SMB signing for both the client and the server side. Signing costs a little throughput on old hardware, which is the trade this makes deliberately.

items.name: Reset Bluetooth Stack
items.description: Restarts the Bluetooth support service and cycles the radio devices, which clears a stack that has stopped enumerating headsets or mice. Paired devices are kept - nothing is unpaired.

items.name: Reset Group Policy Client Cache
items.description: Removes the local group policy history and forces a full refresh, which recovers a client stuck applying a policy that no longer exists. Domain and MDM policy are re-applied from the source; nothing authored centrally is lost.

items.name: Reset Microsoft Store Cache
items.description: Clears the Store cache for the signed-in user with wsreset and re-registers the Store package if it is missing. For devices where the company portal or a Store app will not install and the error is a cache fault rather than a policy.

items.name: Reset OneDrive Client
items.description: Runs the OneDrive reset switch and restarts the client for the signed-in user. Resolves a sync that has stopped without an error; files already uploaded stay in the cloud and are re-linked as the client reconnects.

items.name: Reset Windows Search Index
items.description: Stops the search service, deletes the index database and lets it rebuild. This is the fix for Outlook and Start menu search returning nothing; the rebuild takes hours and search is degraded until it finishes.

items.name: Reset Windows Update Components
items.description: Stops the update services, clears the SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 caches, restarts the services and forces a new detection pass. Fixes stuck or failing Windows Update scans.

items.name: Reset Winsock And TCP/IP Stack
items.description: Resets the Winsock catalog and the IPv4 and IPv6 stacks, which clears a layered service provider or a corrupt TCP/IP registry branch. The change only takes effect at the next restart - the script reports that and does not reboot.

items.name: Restart Audio Services
items.description: Restarts the Windows Audio and Audio Endpoint Builder services in the right order, which recovers a device with no sound after a dock change or a driver update - without the reboot the user is usually told to do.

items.name: Restart Explorer Shell
items.description: Restarts the shell for the signed-in user, which recovers a blank taskbar, a frozen Start menu or missing tray icons without a sign-out. Open File Explorer windows close; applications are left running.

items.name: Restart Stopped Automatic Services
items.description: Starts services set to Automatic that are not running, skipping delayed-start services and a short exclusion list of services that legitimately stop themselves. Every service it starts is named in the log.

items.name: Restart Workspace ONE Hub Services
items.description: Restarts the Hub agent services and, where present, the health monitoring service, then confirms they came back. The first thing to try when a device is enrolled but has stopped checking in.

items.name: Resume BitLocker Protection
items.description: Resumes protection on an OS volume left suspended, which is what a firmware update or a failed servicing operation does. Encryption is untouched; only the suspend state is cleared.

items.name: Resume Windows Update
items.description: Clears an active update pause set in Settings or by a stale policy, and re-enables the update service if it was disabled. The values it clears are logged first so a deliberate pause can be put back.

items.name: Run Component Store Cleanup
items.description: Runs DISM StartComponentCleanup with ResetBase, which removes every superseded component and permanently blocks uninstalling the updates already installed. Long-running - give it the full timeout and do not run it during a patch window.

items.name: Run Defender Quick Scan
items.description: Starts a Defender quick scan on demand and waits, bounded, for it to finish. Meant for the Hub catalog so a user or a technician can run one without an elevated console.

items.name: Run DISM RestoreHealth
items.description: Repairs the component store with DISM /RestoreHealth, which is the prerequisite for SFC to be able to fix anything. Long-running and it needs a source, so it will fail on a device with no path to Windows Update.

items.name: Run Office Quick Repair
items.description: Runs the Click-to-Run quick repair, which replaces damaged program files without re-downloading the whole suite. It closes the Office applications, so run it out of hours or from the catalogue where the user chooses the moment.

items.name: Run SFC Scannow
items.description: Runs System File Checker and reports what it found. Run DISM RestoreHealth first on a device with a damaged component store, or SFC will find corruption it cannot repair.

items.name: Set Crash Dump Type To Small Memory Dump
items.description: Switches the crash dump type to a small memory dump and caps the minidump folder. A full or kernel dump on a 64 GB device can fill the system drive after a single bugcheck; the minidump is enough for a bugcheck code and a faulting module.

items.name: Set Delivery Optimization To LAN Peering
items.description: Sets DODownloadMode to 1 so devices peer within the local subnet only. The safe default for a branch office - it cuts WAN traffic without opening internet peering.

items.name: Set Device Hostname
items.description: Renames the device to a serial-number-based hostname using the ESR_PREFIX variable, then flags a restart as required.

items.name: Set Event Log Size And Retention
items.description: Raises the Application, System and Security log caps to 128 MB with overwrite-as-needed retention. The default 20 MB Security log on a busy device rolls in hours, which is why an investigation so often finds nothing.

items.name: Set Firewall Default Inbound Action To Block
items.description: Sets the default inbound action to Block and outbound to Allow on every firewall profile. Existing allow rules are untouched - this only changes what happens to traffic no rule matches.

items.name: Set Microsoft 365 Update Channel
items.description: Points Click-to-Run at the update channel named in esr_office_channel - Current, MonthlyEnterprise or SemiAnnual - and triggers a channel switch. Moving between channels can be a large download, so stage it.

items.name: Set NTLM Compatibility Level
items.description: Raises LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 so the device sends NTLMv2 only and refuses LM and NTLMv1. Raise this in a pilot first - very old appliances and NAS devices still expect NTLMv1.

items.name: Set NTP Time Source
items.description: Points the Windows Time service at the time source in esr_ntp_server, sets it to the NTP type and resyncs. Only for workgroup or Entra-joined devices - a domain-joined device should take time from the domain hierarchy instead.

items.name: Set Page File To System Managed
items.description: Hands the page file back to Windows after someone has pinned it to a fixed size or disabled it. A missing page file breaks crash dumps and some applications; an oversized fixed one wastes the system drive.

items.name: Set Recovery Actions On Management Services
items.description: Configures restart-on-failure for the Hub, update and Defender services so a crashed agent restarts itself instead of waiting for the next reboot. Sets first, second and subsequent failure to restart after one minute.

items.name: Set Screen Lock Timeout
items.description: Sets the machine inactivity limit to the number of seconds in esr_lock_seconds and requires a password on resume. The registry route applies to every user on the device, including the ones who turned the screen saver off.

items.name: Set Sleep And Display Timeouts
items.description: Applies the display and sleep timeouts in esr_display_minutes and esr_sleep_minutes to the active power plan, on battery and on mains. Use 0 for never - which is the usual choice for sleep on a desk-bound device.

items.name: Set Spooler Service Automatic
items.description: Puts the print spooler back to Automatic and starts it, for devices where a hardening baseline or a PrintNightmare-era workaround disabled printing and nobody put it back.

items.name: Set Time Zone From Variable
items.description: Sets the device time zone to the Windows time zone id in esr_timezone, for example 'Eastern Standard Time'. Useful for kiosks and shared devices that ship with the wrong zone and have no user to correct it.

items.name: Set UAC To Default
items.description: Restores User Account Control to the shipped defaults - prompt on the secure desktop, no silent elevation for administrators. Reverses the local 'turn UAC off' that follows a badly behaved line-of-business installer.

items.name: Trigger Windows Update Scan
items.description: Kicks the update agent into a detection cycle through the scheduled task the OS uses itself, then reports how many updates the agent now knows about. Does not install anything.

items.name: Update Defender Signatures
items.description: Forces a Defender definition update when signatures are more than a day old. Bounded so it cannot sit past the script timeout on a device with no path to the update source.

items.name: Update Microsoft 365 Apps
items.description: Triggers a Click-to-Run update in the background and waits for the updater to finish. Use on devices that have drifted behind the channel baseline because they are rarely restarted or the scheduled task was removed.

items.name: Verify And Salvage The WMI Repository
items.description: Runs winmgmt /verifyrepository and, only if it reports the repository inconsistent, runs a salvage. It never resets the repository outright, because a reset drops third-party MOF registrations and usually costs more than the fault it fixes.

items.name: Archive Stale User Home Folders
items.description: Moves home folders whose owner has not signed in for the days in esr_profile_age_days into a holding folder on the same volume. Never deletes, never touches an account that is currently logged in, and always skips the admin allowlist.

items.name: Clean Homebrew Cache
items.description: Runs a Homebrew cleanup for the signed-in user, removing old formula versions and the download cache. Skips the device entirely where Homebrew is not installed.

items.name: Clear Chrome And Edge Caches
items.description: Closes Chrome and Edge and clears their cache directories for the signed-in user, across every browser profile. Cookies, passwords and profiles are left alone so the user stays signed in.

items.name: Clear Mail Attachment Cache
items.description: Removes the Mail downloads folder, where attachments that were opened but never saved accumulate for years. Messages and saved attachments are untouched - this is the throwaway copy.

items.name: Clear Microsoft Teams Cache
items.description: Closes Teams and removes its cached web content for the signed-in user. Fixes a stuck sign-in or a blank client; chat history lives in the service and is not affected.

items.name: Clear Old Diagnostic Reports
items.description: Removes crash and panic reports older than 60 days from the system and user report folders. Keeps recent ones so an investigation still has something to read.

items.name: Clear Safari Cache
items.description: Closes Safari and clears its cache and web page previews for the signed-in user. History, bookmarks and passwords are untouched, so nothing the user relies on is lost.

items.name: Clear Stuck Print Jobs
items.description: Cancels every queued job and re-enables any queue that has been paused by a failure. Keeps the queues themselves, so this is the gentler alternative to resetting the printing system.

items.name: Clear User Cache Folder
items.description: Removes cached application data older than seven days from the signed-in user's Library Caches. Runs in the user context so it reaches the profile a root script cannot safely write to.

items.name: Clear Xcode Derived Data
items.description: Removes Xcode's derived data and archived device support for the signed-in user. On an engineering Mac this is regularly the largest single reclaimable area, and it is rebuilt automatically on the next build.

items.name: Collect Hub Diagnostic Logs
items.description: Gathers the Hub logs, the MDM profile list and a recent system log extract into one timestamped archive under /var/root, so a technician collects a single file. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is deleted.

items.name: Convert A Mobile Account To Local
items.description: Turns the cached directory account in esr_target_user into a plain local account, keeping the home folder and the UID. The standard move when a Mac leaves a directory it can no longer reach.

items.name: Create A Local Administrator Account
items.description: Creates the hidden local administrator in esr_admin_user with the password in esr_admin_password, if it does not already exist. The account has no secure token, so it cannot unlock FileVault - grant that separately and deliberately.

items.name: Defer Major OS Upgrades
items.description: Sets the major upgrade deferral to the number of days in esr_defer_days, so a new macOS release does not reach the fleet before the applications have been tested. Minor and security updates are unaffected.

items.name: Delete APFS Local Snapshots
items.description: Thins local Time Machine snapshots on the boot volume, then deletes any that remain. Snapshots are the usual reason a disk reports far less free space than the visible files account for.

items.name: Disable AirDrop
items.description: Blocks AirDrop at machine scope and for each existing user. A simple data-movement control on fleets where file sharing is meant to go through managed storage.

items.name: Disable AirPlay Receiver
items.description: Stops the Mac accepting AirPlay from other devices, at machine scope and for each existing user. On a shared floor it stops a laptop appearing as a screen anyone nearby can cast to.

items.name: Disable Apple Remote Desktop
items.description: Deactivates and stops the Apple Remote Desktop agent and removes its access privileges. Use where remote control is provided by another tool and ARD is simply unmanaged surface.

items.name: Disable Automatic Login
items.description: Removes the automatic login user and the stored key file. Automatic login defeats FileVault, because a stolen device boots straight into a signed-in session.

items.name: Disable Content Caching
items.description: Turns off the macOS content cache and flushes what it holds. Deliberate on a site server, accidental on a laptop - where it serves Apple updates to whoever shares the network.

items.name: Disable Diagnostic Analytics Sharing
items.description: Stops the device submitting diagnostic and usage data to Apple and to third-party developers. A privacy-posture setting that is usually decided once centrally and never verified on older builds.

items.name: Disable Guest Account
items.description: Turns off the guest login and guest file sharing. A guest session leaves activity on the device that cannot be attributed to anyone.

items.name: Disable Handoff And Continuity
items.description: Turns off activity advertising and receiving for every local user, so work in progress is not offered to a personal iPhone or iPad standing next to the Mac.

items.name: Disable iCloud Drive Desktop And Documents Sync
items.description: Blocks iCloud Drive and the Desktop and Documents sync feature at machine scope. Stops company documents leaving through a personal Apple account without waiting for a profile to land.

items.name: Disable Internet Sharing
items.description: Stops and disables Internet Sharing, which turns a managed laptop into an unmanaged access point on the corporate network. Rarely deliberate and rarely noticed.

items.name: Disable IPv6 On The Primary Service
items.description: Turns IPv6 off on the network service carrying the default route. A blunt instrument, and the right one where a legacy VPN or an internal service breaks the moment a device prefers IPv6.

items.name: Disable Power Nap
items.description: Turns Power Nap off on all power sources. Power Nap wakes the device to check mail and run backups, which on a laptop in a bag means a warm machine and a flat battery.

items.name: Disable Root Account
items.description: Removes the root account's password so it can no longer be used to log in. Sudo is unaffected - this closes the direct root login that a support session sometimes leaves enabled.

items.name: Disable Screen Sharing
items.description: Unloads and disables the built-in screen sharing service. Reported and handled separately from Apple Remote Desktop, because a device can have either or both.

items.name: Disable Siri
items.description: Blocks Siri at machine scope and hides its menu bar item for each user. On fleets with a voice-assistant restriction this is what makes the restriction real on devices built before the policy.

items.name: Disable SSH Password Authentication
items.description: Where SSH is deliberately in use, forces key-based authentication and refuses root login. Validates the configuration before restarting the service, so a syntax error cannot leave the daemon down.

items.name: Disable SSH Remote Login
items.description: Turns off the SSH server. Inbound SSH is rarely part of a managed Mac support path and is a straightforward lateral movement route when it is left on from a build.

items.name: Disable Wake For Network Access
items.description: Clears Wake for network access so a sleeping laptop stays asleep in a bag. Devices that wake on network traffic overheat in cases and drain overnight, and the setting is on by default.

items.name: Download Software Updates Only
items.description: Downloads pending updates without installing them, so a later install window is short instead of being dominated by the download. Safe to run during the working day.

items.name: Empty Trash
items.description: Empties the signed-in user's Trash and reports how much was reclaimed. The cheapest thing to do first on a disk-full ticket, and entirely reversible only before it runs - so it is offered rather than pushed.

items.name: Enable Application Firewall
items.description: Turns on the macOS application firewall with stealth mode and logging, and allows signed system and downloaded software. Remediates a failed firewall compliance check.

items.name: Enable Automatic App Store Updates
items.description: Turns on automatic download and installation of App Store application updates. Reported separately from system updates because the two settings drift apart and only one is usually in a profile.

items.name: Enable Automatic Security Updates
items.description: Turns on background installation of system data files and security responses, and enables the update check itself. This is the path XProtect definitions arrive by, independent of full OS updates.

items.name: Enable FileVault At Next Login
items.description: Arms deferred FileVault enablement so encryption starts the next time a user signs in, and writes the recovery key to a root-only file for collection. Deferral is the only route that does not need the user's password in the script.

items.name: Enable Firewall Logging
items.description: Turns on application firewall logging so blocked inbound connections leave a record. Without it, a firewall complaint is a matter of opinion rather than evidence.

items.name: Enable Firewall Stealth Mode
items.description: Turns on the application firewall if it is off and enables stealth mode, so the device stops answering probes on closed ports. Existing allowed applications are left alone.

items.name: Enable Gatekeeper
items.description: Turns assessment of downloaded applications back on. Gatekeeper off is almost always a leftover from a one-off install, and it stays off silently for the rest of the device's life.

items.name: Enable Network Time Sync
items.description: Turns on automatic time setting from a network time server. A drifted clock breaks Kerberos, certificate validation and MDM check-in at the same time, and looks like three separate faults.

items.name: Enable Touch ID For Sudo
items.description: Adds the Touch ID PAM module through the sudo_local file, which survives OS upgrades unlike editing the main sudo PAM file. Skips devices with no Touch ID sensor.

items.name: Flush DNS Cache
items.description: Clears the macOS DNS resolver cache and restarts mDNSResponder. Useful after a DNS or VPN configuration change.

items.name: Flush The Directory Service Cache
items.description: Clears the local cache of users, groups and hosts and restarts the directory daemon. Clears the group membership a device is still enforcing after a change, without waiting for the cache to age out.

items.name: Force A Time Resync
items.description: Forces an immediate clock synchronisation against the configured time server and reports the correction. Run before chasing an authentication failure on a device that has been asleep for a long time.

items.name: Force MDM Check-in
items.description: Renews the MDM enrollment profile and triggers a Workspace ONE Intelligent Hub sync so policies, profiles and apps are re-evaluated immediately.

items.name: Install A Package From A URL
items.description: Downloads the installer at esr_pkg_url, checks it against the SHA-256 in esr_pkg_sha256 and installs it. Refuses to install anything whose checksum does not match, so a compromised or truncated download cannot run.

items.name: Install Recommended Software Updates
items.description: Installs every recommended update that does not require a restart, and reports which pending updates were left because they do. Restarts are left to a policy or a device action rather than taken here.

items.name: Install Rosetta 2
items.description: Installs Rosetta 2 non-interactively on Apple silicon so Intel-only line-of-business apps run. Exits cleanly on Intel Macs and when Rosetta is already present.

items.name: Quarantine Unapproved Launch Agents
items.description: Moves machine-scope launch agents and daemons that are not on the allowlist in esr_launch_allowlist into a holding folder under /var/root, so persistence can be removed and reversed. Apple's own items are never touched.

items.name: Quarantine User Launch Agents
items.description: Moves launch agents in the signed-in user's Library that are not in esr_launch_allowlist into a holding folder in their home. User-scope persistence that no machine-scope audit will find.

items.name: Rebuild Kernel Extension Cache
items.description: Rebuilds the boot kernel collection so a device with a stale or damaged cache boots with the drivers it should have. Reports that a restart is needed rather than taking one.

items.name: Rebuild Launch Services Database
items.description: Rebuilds the application registration database, which clears duplicate entries in Open With and file types that open the wrong application. A user-visible fix that costs nothing to run.

items.name: Rebuild The Mail Index
items.description: Closes Mail and removes the envelope index for the signed-in user so it is rebuilt on the next launch. Fixes search that returns nothing and messages that will not open; nothing on the server is affected.

items.name: Reclaim Disk Space
items.description: Removes stale system and per-user caches, empties user trash folders, prunes rotated logs and deletes local Time Machine snapshots, then reports the space recovered.

items.name: Refresh MDM Enrollment Profile
items.description: Asks the device to renew its enrolment profile from the MDM service, which repairs an expired identity certificate without re-enrolling. Does nothing on a device that is not enrolled.

items.name: Remove Application By Bundle Identifier
items.description: Finds the application in /Applications whose bundle identifier matches esr_app_bundle_id and moves it into a holding folder under /var/root rather than deleting it. Reversible, and it leaves evidence of what was removed.

items.name: Remove Configuration Profile By Identifier
items.description: Removes the device-scope configuration profile whose identifier matches esr_profile_identifier. Use to clear a stale profile from a retired management platform that is still fighting the current one.

items.name: Remove Custom Software Update Catalog
items.description: Clears a custom software update catalogue URL so the device talks to Apple again. Devices still pointed at a retired internal update server look healthy and quietly stop receiving updates.

items.name: Remove Old Downloads
items.description: Deletes files in the signed-in user's Downloads folder that have not been touched for the number of days in esr_downloads_age_days. Folders are left alone, so a downloaded project directory is not swept up.

items.name: Remove Passwordless Sudo Entries
items.description: Finds NOPASSWD rules in the sudoers drop-in directory, validates the result and moves the offending files aside. Never edits the main sudoers file, so a mistake cannot lock the device out of administration.

items.name: Remove Proxy Configuration
items.description: Turns off web, secure web, SOCKS and automatic proxy configuration on every network service. Use when a decommissioned proxy is stopping the Hub or software update from reaching the internet.

items.name: Remove Quarantine Attribute
items.description: Clears the com.apple.quarantine attribute from an internally distributed application so it opens without the 'downloaded from the internet' prompt. Restricted to paths under /Applications, so it cannot be aimed at the system.

items.name: Remove SSH Authorized Keys
items.description: Moves every authorized_keys file in a local home and in the root account aside with a timestamp, rather than deleting it. Closes standing key-based access that no directory group controls, and keeps the evidence.

items.name: Remove Stale Printers
items.description: Deletes print queues that are not named in esr_printer_keep. Long-lived Macs accumulate queues for offices nobody visits, and a broken default is a steady source of tickets.

items.name: Remove Stale Wireless Networks
items.description: Removes preferred wireless networks that are not in esr_wifi_keep, so a device stops preferring a hotel or guest SSID over the corporate one. Refuses to run without a keep list.

items.name: Remove Unauthorized Administrators
items.description: Demotes local administrators that are not on the allowlist in esr_admin_allowlist. Accounts are removed from the admin group, never deleted, so the change is reversible and no data is lost.

items.name: Renew DHCP Lease
items.description: Renews the lease on the interface carrying the default route. Uses the interface-level renew rather than cycling the service, so an active remote session is not dropped.

items.name: Repair Home Folder Permissions
items.description: Restores ownership and the standard permissions on the home folder of the user in esr_target_user. The fix after a migration or a restore that has left a user unable to write to their own Desktop.

items.name: Repair Hub Launch Daemon Registration
items.description: Re-enables and bootstraps any Hub launch daemon that has been disabled or unloaded, which is how an agent ends up installed but never running after a cleanup tool has been near the device.

items.name: Require Password After Screen Saver
items.description: Sets every local user to require a password immediately after the screen saver starts. Writes into each user's own preference domain rather than root's, which is the usual mistake when this is scripted.

items.name: Reset Launchpad Layout
items.description: Rebuilds the Launchpad database so removed applications stop appearing and new ones are picked up. A cosmetic fix, and one users raise often after a software migration.

items.name: Reset Network Locations To Automatic
items.description: Switches back to the Automatic network location and removes the extra locations a user or an old support script created. Extra locations are a frequent cause of settings that apply and then mysteriously do not.

items.name: Reset OneDrive Client
items.description: Quits OneDrive, clears its local settings cache and starts it again for the signed-in user. Files already uploaded stay in the cloud and are re-linked as the client reconnects.

items.name: Reset Privacy Permissions For An App
items.description: Resets every TCC privacy grant for the bundle identifier in esr_app_bundle_id, so the application asks again for camera, microphone, screen recording and files. The cure for a permission the user denied once and cannot find how to change.

items.name: Reset Software Update Preferences
items.description: Clears ignored updates and the cached catalogue so a device that has been told to skip an update starts offering it again. Frequently the reason a Mac reports compliant and never patches.

items.name: Reset Spotlight Index
items.description: Turns indexing off and on for the boot volume and erases the existing index so it is rebuilt from scratch. Fixes searches that return nothing while the files are plainly there.

items.name: Reset The Camera Subsystem
items.description: Stops the camera assistant processes so the next application to ask gets a fresh one. The usual fix for a green light that stays on or a camera that reports as in use by nothing.

items.name: Reset The Dock To Defaults
items.description: Removes the signed-in user's Dock layout so it rebuilds from the system default. For a Dock full of question marks after an application cleanup, and for shared devices that need a predictable layout.

items.name: Reset The Printing System
items.description: Removes every print queue and restarts CUPS, which clears the corrupt queue state behind jobs that vanish or printers that will not delete. Queues must be re-added afterwards, so pair it with a printer deployment.

items.name: Restart Automatically After A Power Failure
items.description: Enables automatic restart after a power loss and after a system freeze. For lab machines, digital signage and anything else expected to come back on its own after an outage.

items.name: Restart Dock And Finder
items.description: Restarts the Dock and the Finder for the signed-in user, which recovers a frozen menu bar, a missing Dock or a Finder that will not open a window - without a sign-out.

items.name: Restart The Audio Daemon
items.description: Restarts coreaudiod, which recovers a device with no sound after a dock change or a sample-rate mismatch. Faster and less disruptive than the restart users are usually told to do.

items.name: Restart The Bluetooth Daemon
items.description: Restarts bluetoothd so the stack re-enumerates its peripherals. Pairings are kept - this is the recovery for a device that has stopped seeing a keyboard or headset, not a reset of the pairing list.

items.name: Restart Workspace ONE Hub Agent
items.description: Restarts the Hub's launch daemons and agent processes and confirms one comes back. The first thing to try when a Mac is enrolled but has stopped reporting.

items.name: Rotate FileVault Recovery Key
items.description: Replaces the existing personal recovery key with a new one and writes it to a root-only plist for escrow. Requires the current key to be supplied in esr_filevault_current_key - without it the rotation cannot be authorised.

items.name: Rotate The Local Administrator Password
items.description: Sets a new password for the account in esr_admin_user. Where the account holds a secure token the old password is needed too - supply it in esr_admin_old_password, or the reset will succeed for login and leave the keychain and FileVault behind.

items.name: Run First Aid On The Boot Volume
items.description: Runs a verification pass on the boot volume and logs the result. Verification only - a repair needs the volume unmounted, which is a recovery-mode task rather than something to attempt on a running device.

items.name: Run Microsoft AutoUpdate
items.description: Asks Microsoft AutoUpdate to install everything it has pending for the signed-in user. Runs in the user context because msupdate will not act from a root session.

items.name: Set Computer Name
items.description: Sets the computer name, host name and local host name together from esr_computer_name, so the three do not drift apart. The local host name is sanitised to the characters Bonjour allows.

items.name: Set Computer Name From Serial
items.description: Sets ComputerName, LocalHostName and HostName to ESR_PREFIX plus the hardware serial number so the Mac matches the naming standard in inventory and DNS.

items.name: Set DNS Servers
items.description: Sets the resolvers on the service carrying the default route to the space-separated list in esr_dns_servers, or clears them back to DHCP when the value is 'empty'. Validates each address before applying.

items.name: Set Login Window To Name And Password
items.description: Replaces the list of user pictures at the login window with name and password fields, and hides the local administrative accounts. Stops the login window advertising valid usernames to anyone who opens the lid.

items.name: Set Microsoft AutoUpdate Channel
items.description: Sets the Microsoft AutoUpdate channel to the value in esr_mau_channel and turns automatic download on. Valid channels are Current, Preview, Beta and InsiderFast.

items.name: Set Network Time Server
items.description: Points the device at the time server in esr_ntp_server and enables network time. Use to move devices off a decommissioned internal server that they will otherwise keep asking forever.

items.name: Set Screen Saver Idle Time
items.description: Sets the idle time before the screen saver starts, in seconds, from esr_screensaver_seconds, for every local user. Pairs with the screen lock policy - one starts the saver, the other demands the password.

items.name: Set Sleep And Display Timeouts
items.description: Applies the display and system sleep timeouts in esr_display_minutes and esr_sleep_minutes to every power source. Use 0 for never, which is the usual choice for sleep on a desk-bound device.

items.name: Set The Default Browser
items.description: Sets the signed-in user's default browser to the bundle identifier in esr_browser_bundle_id, for example com.google.chrome. The application must already be installed.

items.name: Set The Default Printer
items.description: Makes the queue named in esr_default_printer the device default, if it exists. Does not create the queue - pair it with a printer deployment that has already put the queue on the device.

items.name: Set The Login Window Banner
items.description: Displays the text in esr_login_banner at the login window. Used where an acceptable-use or monitoring notice has to be shown before anyone signs in.

items.name: Set Time Zone
items.description: Sets the device time zone to the identifier in esr_timezone, for example America/New_York. Validates the value against the list the device accepts before applying it.

items.name: Sync Local Host Name To Computer Name
items.description: Rewrites the Bonjour local host name from the current computer name. Cures the devices that answer to a name like 'Marks-MacBook-Pro-2' on the network while the console shows something else entirely.

items.name: Trigger A Chrome Update Check
items.description: Kicks the Google Keystone daemon so Chrome checks for an update now instead of at its own leisure. Does not force a version - it removes the delay, which is usually the actual problem.

items.name: Truncate Oversized System Logs
items.description: Runs the system log rotation and truncates any file in /private/var/log larger than the megabytes given in esr_log_max_mb. Truncates rather than deletes, so a writer holding the file keeps working.

items.name: Add The Sticky Bit To World Writable Directories
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Finds world-writable directories under /var and /opt without the sticky bit and adds it, so one user cannot delete another's files there. Bounded to those two trees to stay cheap.

items.name: Archive Stale User Home Folders
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Moves home directories whose owner has not logged in for 180 days into a holding folder on the same volume. Never deletes, skips logged-in users and skips anyone in sudo or wheel.

items.name: Blacklist Uncommon Filesystem Modules
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Prevents cramfs, freevxfs, jffs2, hfs, hfsplus and udf from loading. None of them is used on a normal fleet, and each has been a source of kernel vulnerabilities.

items.name: Blacklist USB Storage
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Blacklists the usb-storage module and unloads it if nothing is currently mounted from it. The practical removable-media control on Linux, where there is no single switch.

items.name: Cap The Audit Log Size
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Bounds the audit log at eight files of fifty megabytes and tells auditd to rotate rather than halt when it fills. An unbounded audit log fills the disk; a halting one stops the host.

items.name: Clean Container Images And Volumes
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Prunes stopped containers, dangling images and unused build cache. Named volumes are deliberately left alone, because that is where anything worth keeping lives.

items.name: Clean Temporary Directories
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Removes files in /tmp older than 10 days and in /var/tmp older than 30, skipping anything currently open. Leaves systemd's own private directories alone.

items.name: Clean The Package Cache
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Empties the downloaded package cache, which on a long-lived host is regularly several gigabytes of files that will never be reinstalled from disk.

items.name: Clear Failed Login Counters
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Resets the failed login counters that lock an account out after repeated bad passwords, so a user who has already reset their password can get back in without waiting.

items.name: Clear The Name Service Cache
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Invalidates the nscd caches for passwd, group and hosts. On a host still running nscd this is why a new account or a changed group takes an hour to be visible.

items.name: Clear Thumbnail Caches
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Empties the thumbnail caches in every home directory. On a desktop fleet with shared media these grow to gigabytes and are rebuilt on demand, so nothing is lost.

items.name: Clear User Cache Directories
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Removes files older than 30 days from every home directory's .cache, skipping accounts with an active session so nothing is pulled out from under a running application.

items.name: Collect A Diagnostic Bundle
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Gathers system state, failed units, recent kernel messages, disk and memory figures and the network configuration into one archive under /root. The first thing to ask for on an escalation.

items.name: Collect Hub Diagnostic Logs
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Gathers the Hub logs, the service journal and basic system state into one timestamped archive under /root, so a technician collects a single file. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is deleted.

items.name: Disable Automatic Reboot After Updates
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Stops the automatic update mechanism restarting the host on its own, so reboots belong to a maintenance window rather than to whatever hour the timer fires.

items.name: Disable Core Dumps
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets the hard core limit to zero, stops setuid programs dumping and tells systemd to store nothing. Core files can contain secrets held in memory at the moment of the crash.

items.name: Disable Ctrl-Alt-Delete Reboot
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Masks the systemd target that reboots the host on Ctrl-Alt-Delete at the console. On a shared or rack-mounted machine that key combination is an outage waiting for an elbow.

items.name: Disable Display Manager Automatic Login
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Removes automatic login from GDM, LightDM and SDDM. Automatic login defeats disk encryption at rest, because the machine boots straight into a signed-in session.

items.name: Disable IP Forwarding
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns off IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding and persists it. Refuses to run where a container runtime or a bridge is present, because forwarding is load-bearing there.

items.name: Disable IPv6
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns IPv6 off through sysctl and persists it. A blunt instrument, and the right one where a legacy VPN or an internal service breaks the moment a host prefers IPv6.

items.name: Disable Legacy Network Services
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Stops, disables and masks telnet, rsh, rlogin, tftp and vsftpd where they exist. All of them carry credentials in clear text and none belongs on a current fleet.

items.name: Disable Removable Media Automount
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns off automatic mounting and opening of removable media in the GNOME desktop policy. Pairs with the usb-storage blacklist, which is the harder control of the two.

items.name: Disable SSH Password Authentication
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Forces key-based SSH by writing a drop-in rather than editing the main config, so a package upgrade cannot revert it. Refuses to apply where no account has an authorised key.

items.name: Disable SSH Root Login
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets PermitRootLogin to no through a drop-in, after confirming at least one account can reach root by sudo. Validates the config before reloading so a mistake cannot take SSH down.

items.name: Disable The Avahi Daemon
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Stops, disables and masks avahi. Multicast DNS advertises the host to everyone on the segment and is rarely needed outside a desktop network with shared printers.

items.name: Disable Transparent Huge Pages
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns transparent huge pages off now and at boot through a systemd unit. Standard practice for database and low-latency workloads, where the defragmentation stalls are the problem.

items.name: Enable A Persistent Journal
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Makes the systemd journal survive a reboot by creating /var/log/journal and capping it at 500 MB. Without it the evidence for a crash disappears with the crash.

items.name: Enable Address Space Randomisation
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets kernel.randomize_va_space to full randomisation and persists it. Turned down on some legacy application hosts years ago and never turned back up.

items.name: Enable AppArmor Profiles
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Starts AppArmor and moves any profile in complain mode to enforce. Complain mode is the state worth finding - it looks configured in an audit and enforces nothing.

items.name: Enable Firewall Logging
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns on logging of dropped packets in ufw or firewalld, so a blocked-connection complaint can be answered from a log rather than from opinion.

items.name: Enable The Audit Daemon
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Installs auditd where the package manager can reach it, then enables and starts the service. Without auditd the kernel's audit events go nowhere at all.

items.name: Enable The Host Firewall
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Enables whichever firewall the distribution ships - ufw, firewalld or nftables - without disturbing existing rules, and allows SSH first so the host does not lock itself away.

items.name: Enable The Userspace OOM Daemon
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Enables systemd-oomd so memory pressure is handled by killing the offending cgroup rather than by the kernel killing whatever it happens to find. Skips kernels without pressure stall information.

items.name: Enable Time Synchronisation
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Enables whichever time daemon the host has - chrony or systemd-timesyncd - and turns NTP on. A drifted clock breaks Kerberos, TLS validation and log correlation at once.

items.name: Enable Unattended Security Upgrades
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Turns on the distribution's own automatic security update mechanism - unattended-upgrades on Debian family, dnf-automatic on RHEL family - restricted to security updates and with automatic reboot left off.

items.name: Enforce Weekly Log Rotation
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets logrotate to weekly with four rotations and compression, and runs it once so an already oversized log is dealt with rather than waiting for the next cycle.

items.name: Fix Broken Packages
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Completes half-configured packages and repairs a dependency state that is blocking every future install. Runs the distribution's own repair path rather than forcing anything.

items.name: Flush The DNS Cache
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Clears the resolver cache in systemd-resolved, nscd or dnsmasq, whichever is in use. First move for a host resolving a stale address after a DNS change.

items.name: Force A Time Resync
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Forces an immediate clock correction with whichever daemon is present and reports the offset before and after. Run before chasing an authentication failure on a host that has been suspended.

items.name: Harden Network Kernel Parameters
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Applies the standard network hardening set - no ICMP redirects, no source routing, reverse path filtering, SYN cookies, martian logging - in one persisted sysctl file.

items.name: Harden SSH Ciphers And MACs
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Restricts SSH to modern ciphers, MACs and key exchange algorithms through a drop-in. Validates the result before reloading, because a typo here locks everyone out at once.

items.name: Harden The Temp Mount Options
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Adds nodev, nosuid and noexec to /tmp and /dev/shm and remounts them, so a dropped payload in a world-writable directory cannot be executed. Skips /tmp where it is not a separate mount.

items.name: Install And Enable Fail2ban
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Installs fail2ban, enables the SSH jail and starts it. On an internet-facing host this is the difference between a brute force attempt being slowed and running all night.

items.name: Install Baseline Audit Rules
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Writes a small audit ruleset covering identity files, sudoers, the audit configuration itself and privilege escalation, then reloads. Deliberately short so the log stays readable.

items.name: Install Pending Security Updates
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Installs only the updates the package manager marks as security, waiting politely for the package lock rather than removing it. Reports whether a restart is now required and takes none.

items.name: Limit SSH Authentication Attempts
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Caps authentication attempts and sessions per connection and shortens the login grace period, which cuts the value of a brute force attempt without touching the firewall.

items.name: Lock Accounts With An Empty Password
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Locks any account whose shadow password field is empty. These accept a login with no credential at all, so this runs on a schedule rather than once.

items.name: Lock Extra UID Zero Accounts
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Locks any account with UID 0 other than root itself. A second UID 0 account is a root by another name and a common persistence trick; locking is reversible, deleting is not.

items.name: Lock Inactive Accounts
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Locks interactive accounts that have not logged in for 90 days, skipping root and anything in sudo or wheel so an administrator cannot be locked out by their own schedule.

items.name: Mask Unused Desktop Services On Servers
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. On a host with no desktop environment, masks avahi, cups and bluetooth. Refuses to run where a display manager is present, because on a workstation these are wanted.

items.name: Purge Configuration Of Removed Packages
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Purges packages left in the removed-but-configured state on Debian family hosts, which is where old configuration files and their leftover users quietly persist.

items.name: Raise The File Descriptor Limits
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Raises the open file limit for interactive sessions and for systemd services. A host at the limit starts refusing connections in ways that look exactly like a network fault.

items.name: Rebuild The Initramfs
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Regenerates the initial ramdisk for every installed kernel, which is what repairs a host that will not boot after a driver or encryption change. Reports that a restart is needed and takes none.

items.name: Reclaim Disk Space
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. A single pass over the usual offenders - package cache, journal, rotated logs, old temporary files and orphaned packages - reporting how much each one gave back. For a disk-full ticket in a hurry.

items.name: Record And Compare The SUID Baseline
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Writes a list of set-uid binaries to /var/lib and compares it with the previous run, logging anything that has appeared or gone. Reports only - it never changes a permission on its own.

items.name: Refresh Package Metadata
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Refreshes the package index so a pending-update sensor reads current data. Never installs anything, and waits for the lock rather than fighting it.

items.name: Refresh The Desktop Application Database
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Rebuilds the desktop entry, MIME and icon caches so newly installed applications appear in the menu and file associations start working again.

items.name: Remove Old Kernels
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Keeps the running kernel and the two newest and removes the rest, which is what stops a separate /boot partition filling and blocking the next kernel update.

items.name: Remove Old Rotated Log Files
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Deletes rotated and compressed log files under /var/log older than 90 days. Only touches files that already carry a rotation suffix, so an active log is never removed.

items.name: Remove Old Snap Revisions
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Removes disabled snap revisions, which each keep a full copy of the application on disk. On a desktop fleet this is often the single largest reclaimable area.

items.name: Remove Orphaned Packages
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Removes packages that were pulled in as dependencies and are no longer needed by anything. Uses the package manager's own autoremove, so nothing explicitly installed is touched.

items.name: Remove Passwordless Sudo Entries
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Moves sudoers drop-in files containing NOPASSWD into a holding directory and validates the result with visudo, restoring them if the sudoers set no longer parses.

items.name: Remove SSH Authorized Keys
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Moves every authorized_keys file in a home directory and in root aside with a timestamp rather than deleting it, closing standing key access while keeping the evidence of what was there.

items.name: Remove The Proxy Environment
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Clears proxy variables from the system environment and from the package manager's own configuration. Use when a decommissioned proxy is stopping updates or agent check-in.

items.name: Remove Unapproved User Cron Jobs
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Moves user crontabs aside for accounts outside the approved list, keeping a copy under /root. User cron is persistence nobody audits and scheduling nobody documents.

items.name: Renew The DHCP Lease
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Renews the lease on the interface carrying the default route. Refuses to run over SSH on that same interface, because a release-and-renew there ends the session that started it.

items.name: Repair The Hub Service Registration
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Re-enables and starts a Hub service that has been disabled or masked, which is how an agent ends up installed but never running after a hardening pass has been over the host.

items.name: Report Disk Health
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Reads SMART health, reallocated sector count and wear indicators for every physical disk and logs them. Reporting only, because a failing disk needs a replacement rather than a script.

items.name: Report Read Only Mounts
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Finds local filesystems the kernel has remounted read-only after an error and logs them with the last relevant kernel message. Deliberately does not remount, because that hides a failing disk.

items.name: Restart Failed Systemd Units
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Restarts units in the failed state once and reports which recovered. Skips one-shot units and anything that has already failed to restart repeatedly, so it cannot become a restart loop.

items.name: Restart SSSD And Clear Its Cache
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Clears the SSSD cache and restarts the daemon, so a group membership or account change in the directory takes effect now rather than when the cache ages out.

items.name: Restart The Container Runtime
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Restarts the container daemon and reports how many containers came back. Refuses where containers have no restart policy, because restarting the daemon would leave them stopped.

items.name: Restart The Display Manager
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Restarts the graphical login manager, which recovers a host stuck at a blank or frozen login screen. Refuses to run while anyone has a graphical session, because it ends those sessions.

items.name: Restart The Network Stack
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Restarts NetworkManager or systemd-networkd and confirms the default route came back. Refuses to run over an active SSH session, because that is exactly how a remote host is lost.

items.name: Restart The Workspace ONE Hub Agent
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Restarts the Hub service and confirms it came back. The first thing to try when a Linux endpoint is enrolled but has stopped reporting to the console.

items.name: Restore The Resolver Configuration Symlink
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Points /etc/resolv.conf back at systemd-resolved after someone has replaced it with a static file. The reason a DNS change made by hand keeps reverting, or never takes at all.

items.name: Restrict SSH To Administrative Groups
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Limits SSH to members of sudo, wheel and a dedicated sshusers group through a drop-in. Confirms at least one member exists first, so the host does not become unreachable.

items.name: Resubmit Expiring Machine Certificates
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Asks certmonger to renew any tracked certificate that is not in the MONITORING state. The usual cure for a host that has quietly dropped out of a certificate-authenticated service.

items.name: Rotate SSH Host Keys
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Regenerates the host keys, which is what a machine cloned from an image needs so it stops presenting the same identity as every other host from that image. Existing sessions are not dropped.

items.name: Schedule A Filesystem Check At Next Boot
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Requests a filesystem check on the next restart rather than attempting one on a mounted volume. The safe way to act on a filesystem that has started reporting errors.

items.name: Set Password Aging Policy
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets PASS_MAX_DAYS to 365, PASS_MIN_DAYS to 1 and PASS_WARN_AGE to 14 in login.defs, and applies the same to existing interactive accounts so the policy is not only true for new ones.

items.name: Set SELinux To Enforcing
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Moves SELinux from permissive to enforcing and persists it. Refuses where SELinux is fully disabled, because that needs a relabel and a reboot rather than a one-line change.

items.name: Set The Default Umask
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets a 027 umask in login.defs and a profile drop-in, so newly created files are not world readable. Existing files are untouched - this changes what happens from now on.

items.name: Set The Firewall Default To Deny Inbound
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets the default inbound policy to deny and outbound to allow, leaving existing allow rules in place. Confirms SSH is still permitted before applying, so a remote host stays reachable.

items.name: Set The GNOME Screen Lock Policy
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Locks the screen after five minutes of idle time for every GNOME user through a dconf system database, so it applies to accounts that do not exist yet as well as those that do.

items.name: Set The Hostname From Inventory
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets the static hostname from the ESR_HOSTNAME environment variable, or from the DMI serial number when that is not set, and keeps /etc/hosts consistent with it.

items.name: Set The Login Banner
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Writes an authorised-use notice to /etc/issue, /etc/issue.net and /etc/motd and points sshd at it, so the notice is shown on console and remote logins alike.

items.name: Set The NTP Servers
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Points chrony or systemd-timesyncd at the servers in the ESR_NTP_SERVERS environment variable, space separated, defaulting to the pool. Backs the existing configuration up first.

items.name: Set The Time Zone
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets the time zone from the ESR_TIMEZONE environment variable, defaulting to UTC. On a fleet where jobs are scheduled locally a wrong zone silently moves every scheduled action.

items.name: Set Virtual Memory Swappiness
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Sets vm.swappiness to 10 so the kernel prefers reclaiming cache over swapping application memory. Skips hosts with no swap, where the setting means nothing.

items.name: Sync The Hosts File With The Hostname
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Makes sure the current hostname resolves locally by fixing the 127.0.1.1 entry. A hostname with no matching hosts entry makes sudo pause for seconds on every single command.

items.name: Trim Filesystems
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Runs a discard pass across mounted filesystems so an SSD or a thin-provisioned volume gets its freed blocks back. Skips hosts with no trim-capable mount rather than erroring.

items.name: Update Flatpak Applications
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Updates installed flatpaks and removes unused runtimes. Flatpaks sit outside the package manager, so without this they are never patched by the normal update cycle.

items.name: Update Snap Packages
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Refreshes installed snaps and holds the retention at two revisions. Snaps update on their own schedule, so this exists to make that schedule predictable rather than to replace it.

items.name: Update The Boot Loader Configuration
items.description: Delivery: ad hoc. Regenerates the GRUB configuration so newly installed kernels appear in the boot menu. Backs up the existing configuration first, because an empty menu is an unbootable host.

items.name: Update The CA Certificate Store
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Rebuilds the system trust store so certificates dropped into the local anchors directory take effect. The fix for a host that trusts an internal CA everywhere except in one tool.

items.name: Vacuum The Systemd Journal
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Trims the journal to 500 MB and 30 days, which is what stops an unbounded journal quietly filling the root volume on a long-lived host.

items.name: Verify Package File Integrity
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Verifies installed package files against the package database and logs anything whose contents no longer match. Reports only - it never replaces a file on its own.

items.name: Write An Inventory Snapshot
items.description: Delivery: systemd timer. Writes a compact inventory of the host - platform, kernel, hardware, memory, disk, package and agent state - to a file another tool or a sensor can read without running a dozen commands.

items.name: Write The Support Contact Message
items.description: Delivery: packaged post-install. Puts the hostname, the build date and a support contact into the message of the day, so whoever logs in at three in the morning knows which host they are on and who owns it.

items.name: AC Power Connected
