items.description: Console sensor name: ac_power_connected. True when the device is on mains power at sample time. Useful as a second condition on anything you do not want running on battery, such as a feature update or a full scan.

items.name: Active Network Category
items.description: Console sensor name: active_network_category. Closed set: DomainAuthenticated, Private, Public, Mixed, None. A device sitting on Public sees the strictest firewall profile, which is the quiet cause of most 'it works at the office' tickets.

items.name: Active Power Plan
items.description: Console sensor name: active_power_plan. Closed set: Balanced, HighPerformance, PowerSaver, UltimatePerformance, Custom. Matched on the scheme GUID rather than the display name, so a localised device still groups correctly.

items.name: Application Crashes (7 Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: application_crashes_7d. Application Error events in the last seven days. The absolute number matters less than which devices sit in the tail - those are the ones with a broken profile or a bad add-in.

items.name: ASR Rules In Block Mode
items.description: Console sensor name: asr_rules_in_block_mode. How many Attack Surface Reduction rules are set to Block (action 1). Audit-mode and unconfigured rules are not counted, so this is the honest measure of ASR coverage.

items.name: Autologon Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: autologon_configured. True when AutoAdminLogon is set with a stored username. Usually a leftover from imaging or a kiosk build, and it often leaves the password in the registry in clear text.

items.name: Battery Cycle Count
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_cycle_count. Charge cycles the battery reports. Many OEM batteries return 0 because the firmware does not expose the counter - treat 0 as unreported rather than as new, and use battery health for those.

items.name: Battery Health Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_health_percent. Full-charge capacity as a percentage of the battery's design capacity. Returns -1 on desktops and on hardware that does not expose the WMI battery classes, so filter on Battery Present first.

items.name: Battery Present
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_present. True when the device reports a battery. Ship this alongside every other battery sensor so desktops answer 'not applicable' here instead of polluting a health or cycle-count average.

items.name: BIOS Age (Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: bios_age_days. Days since the installed firmware was released, from the BIOS release date. A clean way to find the devices a firmware update policy has never actually reached.

items.name: BIOS Version
items.description: Console sensor name: bios_version. Firmware version string from the system BIOS. Combined with the model, this is what tells you which devices a firmware-fixed issue still applies to.

items.name: BitLocker Encryption Percentage
items.description: Console sensor name: bitlocker_encryption_percentage. How far the OS volume has encrypted, 0-100. Returns -1 when BitLocker is unavailable. Catches devices stuck part-way through encryption, which read as protected in most reports.

items.name: BitLocker Protection Status
items.description: Returns true when the OS volume is fully encrypted and protection is on.

items.name: BitLocker Protector Type
items.description: Console sensor name: bitlocker_protector_type. Closed set: TpmAndPin, TpmOnly, PasswordOnly, Other, None. Separates devices meeting a pre-boot authentication standard from those relying on TPM alone.

items.name: BitLocker Recovery Password Present
items.description: Console sensor name: bitlocker_recovery_password_present. True when the OS volume carries a RecoveryPassword key protector. A device encrypted without one cannot be recovered and is the fleet's real BitLocker risk.

items.name: Boot Duration (Seconds)
items.description: Console sensor name: boot_duration_seconds. How long the last boot took, from the Diagnostics-Performance operational log, in whole seconds. Returns -1 where that log is disabled. The number a user means when they say the machine is slow.

items.name: BranchCache Service State
items.description: Console sensor name: branchcache_service_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. Worth counting on branch-office devices where BranchCache is meant to be carrying content but the service never starts.

items.name: Built-in Administrator Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: builtin_administrator_enabled. True when the well-known RID 500 account is enabled. Matched on the SID rather than the name so a renamed Administrator account is still caught.

items.name: Chassis Type
items.description: Console sensor name: chassis_type. Closed set: Laptop, Desktop, Tablet, VirtualMachine, Server, Other. Form factor decides which policies make sense, and virtual machines should be excluded from most hardware sensors.

items.name: Chrome Browser Version
items.description: Console sensor name: chrome_browser_version. File version of the installed Google Chrome binary, or NotInstalled. Chrome that has not moved in weeks usually means the updater task was disabled or the device is off the network Google needs.

items.name: Crash Dump Present
items.description: Console sensor name: crash_dump_present. True when a full memory dump or at least one minidump is on disk. It is both the evidence for a bugcheck investigation and, for MEMORY.DMP, often several gigabytes of reclaimable space.

items.name: Credential Guard Status
items.description: Console sensor name: credential_guard_status. Closed set: Running, Configured, NotConfigured, NotApplicable. Configured-but-not-running is the interesting state - the policy landed but the hardware or a driver blocked it.

items.name: Days Since Last Reboot
items.description: Whole days since the last boot. Surfaces the long-uptime devices that never finish patch installs.

items.name: Days Since Last Update Install
items.description: Console sensor name: days_since_last_update_install. Days since Windows Update last recorded a successful install, from the Auto Update Results key. Returns -1 when the key is absent, which itself means the agent has never completed an install.

items.name: Defender Active Threat Count
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_active_threat_count. Number of threats Defender still considers active (not cleaned, quarantined or allowed). Returns -1 when Defender is unavailable. Non-zero means a device needs a human.

items.name: Defender Cloud Protection Level
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_cloud_protection_level. Closed set: Advanced, Basic, Disabled. Cloud-delivered protection is what catches the first hour of a new campaign; a Disabled here is a real gap, not a preference.

items.name: Defender Days Since Full Scan
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_days_since_full_scan. Days since the last completed full scan; -1 when Defender is unavailable or has never run one. Use it to find the devices a monthly full-scan policy never actually reaches.

items.name: Defender Platform Version
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_platform_version. The Defender anti-malware platform version string. Platform updates ship separately from definitions and a stuck platform is a common cause of features silently not applying.

items.name: Defender Real-Time Protection Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_realtime_protection_enabled. True when Microsoft Defender real-time protection is on. False on devices where a user or a stale third-party AV left the engine passive.

items.name: Defender Signature Age (Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_signature_age_days. Days since the antivirus definitions were last updated. Returns -1 when Defender is not the active engine. Anything over 3 is a device that has not reached the update path in a week of business days.

items.name: Defender Tamper Protection Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: defender_tamper_protection_enabled. True when tamper protection is active. Tamper protection is what stops a local admin or a script disabling Defender, so a false here undermines every other Defender sensor.

items.name: Delivery Optimization Mode
items.description: Console sensor name: delivery_optimization_mode. Closed set: HttpOnly, LanPeering, GroupPeering, InternetPeering, SimpleBypass, BypassDO, Default. Effective DODownloadMode drives whether peering is doing anything for your bandwidth at all.

items.name: Device Join Type
items.description: Console sensor name: device_join_type. Closed set: HybridJoined, EntraJoined, DomainJoined, EntraRegistered, Workgroup. Read from dsregcmd state in the registry rather than by shelling out, so it stays inside a sensor's time budget.

items.name: Device Manager Error Count
items.description: Console sensor name: device_manager_error_count. How many PnP devices are present but in an error state. This is the yellow-triangle count, and it is the fastest single number for finding a bad driver rollout.

items.name: Edge Browser Version
items.description: Console sensor name: edge_browser_version. File version of the installed Microsoft Edge binary, or NotInstalled. Edge updates itself, so the spread here is a direct measure of which devices its updater cannot reach.

items.name: Expired Machine Certificates
items.description: Console sensor name: expired_machine_certificates. How many expired certificates are still sitting in the machine personal store. They do not break anything on their own but they are what makes certificate troubleshooting take an hour.

items.name: Failed Scheduled Tasks
items.description: Console sensor name: failed_scheduled_tasks. Enabled scheduled tasks whose last run returned a non-zero result, ignoring the 0x41301 'still running' code. Catches maintenance, inventory and agent tasks that stopped working months ago.

items.name: Fast Startup Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: fast_startup_enabled. True when hybrid shutdown is on, which means a user's shutdown does not clear uptime or apply a pending servicing operation. It is the usual reason a device shows 40 days of uptime and a stuck update.

items.name: Firewall Inbound Allow Rules
items.description: Console sensor name: firewall_inbound_allow_rules. Count of enabled inbound Allow rules in the active firewall store. A device far above the fleet median has usually collected rules from an application install or a local admin.

items.name: Firewall Profiles Disabled
items.description: Console sensor name: firewall_profiles_disabled. Closed set: None, Domain, Private, Public, Multiple. Names which Windows Firewall profile is switched off rather than just flagging that one is - the profile tells you where the device was when it happened.

items.name: Free Disk Space (GB)
items.description: Whole gigabytes free on the system drive. Drives the low-disk smart group used to target cleanup scripts before feature updates.

items.name: Guest Account Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: guest_account_enabled. True when the RID 501 Guest account is enabled. Rare but it happens after an imaging or a third-party kiosk tool, and it is a standard audit failure.

items.name: Hibernation Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: hibernation_enabled. True when hiberfil.sys is active. On a small system drive the hibernation file is often several gigabytes that nobody has decided to spend, and it is a prerequisite for fast startup.

items.name: Hub Agent Version
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_agent_version. Installed Workspace ONE Intelligent Hub version, or Unknown when the agent is not present. Version spread across a fleet is what turns 'the sensor does not report' into a known Hub-version floor.

items.name: Hub Log Age (Hours)
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_log_age_hours. Hours since anything was written to the Hub log folder, as a proxy for the last real check-in. Returns -1 when the folder is missing. A device above 24 has stopped talking even if the console still shows it online.

items.name: Hub Service Running
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_service_running. True when the Workspace ONE Intelligent Hub service is present and in the Running state. A stopped Hub is why a device stops taking scripts, sensors and profiles while still looking enrolled.

items.name: IPv6 Disabled
items.description: Console sensor name: ipv6_disabled. True when DisabledComponents has IPv6 switched off across interfaces. Fleets that disabled IPv6 years ago break Teams media paths and DirectAccess without anyone connecting the two.

items.name: LAPS Password Age (Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: laps_password_age_days. Days since Windows LAPS last rotated the managed local account password, from the LAPS state key. Returns -1 where Windows LAPS is not in use - legacy Microsoft LAPS keeps its expiry in AD, not on the device.

items.name: Largest Outlook OST (GB)
items.description: Console sensor name: largest_outlook_ost_gb. Size of the biggest Outlook offline data file across all local profiles, rounded to whole gigabytes. Files past about 40 GB are where Outlook search and sync start failing in ways users describe as 'slow'.

items.name: Last Boot Time
items.description: Console sensor name: last_boot_time. UTC timestamp of the last real boot, in ISO 8601. Every device has one, so a DateTime sensor is safe here - there is no unknown case to encode.

items.name: LLMNR Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: llmnr_enabled. True when LLMNR name resolution is still available, which is the case unless policy has set EnableMulticast to 0. LLMNR and NBT-NS poisoning is how credentials leave a flat network.

items.name: Local Accounts With Non-Expiring Password
items.description: Console sensor name: local_accounts_never_expire. Count of enabled local accounts whose password never expires, excluding the disabled built-ins. Service accounts created by an installer are the usual finding.

items.name: Local Administrator Count
items.description: Console sensor name: local_administrator_count. How many members the local Administrators group holds, including domain and Entra groups counted as one member each. Devices well above the fleet norm have collected standing admin rights.

items.name: LSA Protection Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: lsa_protection_enabled. True when LSASS runs as a protected process (RunAsPPL). The single cheapest credential-theft mitigation, and one that quietly reverts on some in-place upgrades.

items.name: Machine Certificate Minimum Days
items.description: Console sensor name: machine_certificate_min_days. Fewest days remaining on any currently valid machine certificate that has a private key. Returns -1 when the store holds none. This is the number that predicts a Wi-Fi or VPN outage a month out.

items.name: MDM Enrollment Healthy
items.description: Console sensor name: mdm_enrollment_healthy. True when an enrollment under HKLM Enrollments reports EnrollmentState 1 and still has its EnterpriseMgmt scheduled tasks. Catches the half-unenrolled device that keeps reporting inventory but never applies policy.

items.name: Memory In Use Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: memory_in_use_percent. Percentage of physical memory committed at the moment the sensor sampled. One reading is noise; the distribution across a fleet, sampled repeatedly, is what identifies the under-specified models.

items.name: Memory Integrity Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: memory_integrity_enabled. True when HVCI (hypervisor-protected code integrity) is running. The usual blocker is an incompatible driver, so pair this with the unsigned driver count.

items.name: NTLMv1 Allowed
items.description: Console sensor name: ntlmv1_allowed. True when LmCompatibilityLevel is below 3, so the device may still send LM or NTLMv1 responses. Absent value reads as the OS default, which is level 3 on supported builds.

items.name: Office Update Channel
items.description: Console sensor name: office_update_channel. Closed set: Current, MonthlyEnterprise, SemiAnnual, SemiAnnualPreview, CurrentPreview, Beta, NotInstalled. Matched on the channel GUID, because the friendly names have been renamed twice.

items.name: Office Version
items.description: Console sensor name: office_version. Click-to-Run build number for installed Microsoft 365 Apps, or NotInstalled. The build is what a known Outlook or Excel regression is actually keyed on, not the marketing year.

items.name: OneDrive Known Folder Move Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: onedrive_kfm_configured. True when Known Folder Move policy is set on the device. Without it, Desktop and Documents are not backed up, which is the difference between a re-image and a data loss incident.

items.name: OS Install Age (Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: os_install_age_days. Days since the current Windows build was installed, which a feature update resets. High values on a fleet that should be current are devices a feature update has never reached.

items.name: Page File Configuration
items.description: Console sensor name: page_file_configuration. Closed set: SystemManaged, Custom, None, Multiple. A device with no page file will not write a crash dump, which is how a recurring bugcheck stays undiagnosable.

items.name: Pending Reboot Required
items.description: Returns true when servicing, Windows Update or a pending file rename is waiting on a restart. Targets reboot prompts at only the devices that need one.

items.name: Pending Update Count
items.description: Console sensor name: pending_update_count. Number of applicable, not-yet-installed updates from the Windows Update agent's cached results. The search runs offline so the sensor never touches the network; a device that has never scanned returns -1.

items.name: Physical Memory (GB)
items.description: Console sensor name: physical_memory_gb. Installed RAM rounded to the nearest whole gigabyte. The simplest way to find the 4 and 8 GB devices that will not survive the next Teams and Office baseline.

items.name: PowerShell v2 Engine Present
items.description: Console sensor name: powershell_v2_engine_present. True when the PowerShell 2.0 engine is still installed. The v2 engine bypasses script block logging and AMSI, so it is a standard audit finding long after anyone stopped using it.

items.name: Print Spooler State
items.description: Console sensor name: print_spooler_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. Disabled is a legitimate hardening choice on servers and a broken printing experience on a laptop, so read it against the device's role.

items.name: Processor Load Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: processor_load_percent. Average processor load across all sockets at sample time, 0-100. Treat it as a fleet distribution rather than a per-device truth - a single sample catches whatever was running that second.

items.name: Proxy Configuration
items.description: Console sensor name: proxy_configuration. Closed set: None, Manual, AutoConfig, Both. Read from the machine-wide Internet Settings and policy keys, so it reflects what a SYSTEM-context process such as the Hub will actually use.

items.name: RDP Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: rdp_enabled. True when Remote Desktop connections are permitted. On a client fleet this should normally be a small, named set of devices; anything else is drift or a helpdesk workaround left behind.

items.name: RDP Network Level Authentication Required
items.description: Console sensor name: rdp_nla_required. True when RDP requires Network Level Authentication. Only meaningful where RDP is enabled, so pair it with that sensor rather than reading a false on a device with RDP off as a finding.

items.name: Reboot Pending Reason
items.description: Console sensor name: reboot_pending_reason. Closed set: None, ComponentBasedServicing, WindowsUpdate, PendingFileRename, ComputerRename, Multiple. Says why a restart is owed, which is what decides whether it can wait for the maintenance window.

items.name: Recycle Bin Size (MB)
items.description: Console sensor name: recycle_bin_size_mb. Total size of every user's recycle bin on the system drive, in whole megabytes. Frequently the single largest thing a disk-space script can reclaim without touching live data.

items.name: Secure Boot Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: secure_boot_enabled. True when the firmware reports Secure Boot active. Legacy BIOS and CSM devices return false and are the ones blocking a Windows 11 or Credential Guard rollout.

items.name: SMB Signing Required
items.description: Console sensor name: smb_signing_required. True when the SMB server requires packet signing. Required signing is what defeats SMB relay; enabled-but-not-required is the state most fleets are actually in.

items.name: SMBv1 Client Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: smbv1_client_enabled. True when the mrxsmb10 driver is set to start, meaning the device can still speak SMBv1 to a server. Read from the service start type so the sensor stays fast and does not touch DISM.

items.name: Stale User Profile Count
items.description: Console sensor name: stale_user_profile_count. Non-system profiles not loaded in the last 90 days and not currently in use. This is the number the profile cleanup script should reduce, and the safe subset to act on.

items.name: Stopped Automatic Services
items.description: Console sensor name: stopped_automatic_services. Count of services set to start automatically that are not running, excluding delayed-start services that legitimately start late. A device far above the fleet norm has something failing at boot.

items.name: Storage Sense Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: storage_sense_enabled. True when Storage Sense is configured to run. Where it is on, low-disk tickets tend to be about something other than temp files - which changes what the fix should be.

items.name: Stuck Print Jobs
items.description: Console sensor name: stuck_print_jobs. Files sitting in the spooler's PRINTERS folder, which is what a queue jammed in Deleting or Error state looks like on disk. Counted rather than inspected so the sensor stays fast on a busy print client.

items.name: System Drive Free Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: system_drive_free_percent. Free space on the system drive as a whole percentage. A percentage groups a mixed fleet of 128 GB and 1 TB devices into one meaningful smart group where a raw GB figure does not.

items.name: System Drive Health Status
items.description: Console sensor name: system_drive_health_status. Closed set: Healthy, Warning, Unhealthy, Unknown. The storage stack's own view of the physical disk holding Windows - the earliest warning you get before a device stops booting.

items.name: System Drive Media Type
items.description: Console sensor name: system_drive_media_type. Closed set: SSD, HDD, Unspecified, Unknown. Spinning disks left in a fleet are the devices where every patch window and every logon takes three times as long.

items.name: Third-Party Antivirus Present
items.description: Console sensor name: third_party_antivirus_present. True when Security Center registers an antivirus product other than Microsoft Defender. This is what puts Defender into passive mode, and it explains most 'Defender is off' reports.

items.name: Time Offset (Seconds)
items.description: Console sensor name: time_offset_seconds. Absolute phase offset the Windows Time service last measured against its source, rounded to whole seconds. Read from the local service state, so the sensor never touches the network. Kerberos starts failing around 300.

items.name: Time Service State
items.description: Console sensor name: time_service_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. W32Time set to Manual and not running is the default on workgroup devices and the reason their clocks drift until Kerberos or certificate validation fails.

items.name: TPM Ready State
items.description: Returns true when a TPM is present, enabled and ready for use. Identifies devices that cannot take BitLocker, Credential Guard or Windows 11.

items.name: Unexpected Shutdowns (30 Days)
items.description: Console sensor name: unexpected_shutdowns_30d. Kernel-Power 41 events in the last 30 days - power loss, bugcheck or a hard hang. Two or more on a laptop is a hardware conversation, not a software one.

items.name: Update Cache Size (MB)
items.description: Console sensor name: update_cache_size_mb. Size of the SoftwareDistribution download folder in whole megabytes. A cache that keeps growing past a few GB usually means downloads that install and are never cleaned, or an update that fails on every attempt.

items.name: User Profile Count
items.description: Console sensor name: user_profile_count. How many non-system user profiles exist on the device. Shared and hot-desk machines accumulate profiles until the system drive fills, and the count is the cheap early warning.

items.name: Virtualization Based Security Status
items.description: Console sensor name: vbs_status. Closed set: Running, Enabled, Disabled, NotApplicable. VBS is the floor under Credential Guard and memory integrity, so check it before chasing either of those.

items.name: VPN Profile Count
items.description: Console sensor name: vpn_profile_count. How many all-user VPN profiles are provisioned on the device. Per-user profiles are not counted because a sensor running as SYSTEM cannot see them - say so before someone reads a zero as 'no VPN'.

items.name: WDAC Enforcement Status
items.description: Console sensor name: wdac_enforcement_status. Closed set: Enforced, AuditOnly, Off, NotApplicable. Application Control policies that silently fell back to audit mode after a servicing update are invisible until you count them.

items.name: Windows Activation Status
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_activation_status. Closed set: Licensed, OutOfGrace, Notification, Unlicensed, Other. Reads the Windows operating-system licence only, so an Office licence state cannot skew the reading.

items.name: Windows Build Version
items.description: Edition, feature release and full build number including the UBR, for example 'Windows 11 Pro 24H2 (26100.1742)'. Gives patch reporting a single accurate version string.

items.name: Windows Edition
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_edition. The SKU name, for example Enterprise, Professional or Education. Edition drives which of BitLocker, WDAC, Credential Guard and AppLocker a device can actually take.

items.name: Windows Search Service State
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_search_service_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. A stopped WSearch is the answer to almost every 'Outlook search finds nothing' ticket, and it is invisible from the application side.

items.name: Windows Temp Size (MB)
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_temp_size_mb. Size of the machine temp folder in whole megabytes. Pairs with the disk cleanup script: measure it, clean it, and watch the number come down rather than guessing at how much was recovered.

items.name: Windows Update Paused
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_update_paused. True when feature or quality updates are paused by policy or by a user in Settings, and the pause has not yet expired. A paused device looks compliant to anything that only counts pending updates.

items.name: Windows Update Service State
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_update_service_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. A wuauserv set to Disabled is the most common reason a device reports zero missing updates forever.

items.name: Windows.old Present
items.description: Console sensor name: windows_old_present. True when a Windows.old folder from a feature update is still on the system drive. It is typically 15-25 GB and Windows only removes it automatically for the first ten days.

items.name: WinRM Service State
items.description: Console sensor name: winrm_service_state. Closed set: Running, Stopped, Disabled, Missing. WinRM left running on a client fleet widens the lateral movement surface; WinRM stopped where your tooling depends on it is an outage waiting to be discovered.

items.name: Wireless Signal Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: wireless_signal_percent. Signal quality of the connected wireless interface, 0-100, or -1 when there is no wireless link. Parsed as a bare percentage from netsh so a localised console still reports a number.

items.name: WSUS Server Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: wsus_server_configured. True when a WUServer policy points the device at an on-premises update server. Devices that should have moved to Windows Update for Business often still carry the old policy from a stale GPO.

items.name: AC Power Connected
items.description: Console sensor name: ac_power_connected. True when the device is drawing from mains. Worth having before pushing an upgrade or a long-running task to a fleet of laptops.

items.name: Activation Lock Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: activation_lock_enabled. True when Activation Lock is on. On a corporate device this blocks reprovisioning unless the bypass code was escrowed, so it is worth finding before the device comes back from a leaver rather than after.

items.name: Administrator Account Count
items.description: Console sensor name: admin_user_count. Number of accounts in the local admin group, excluding the hidden management accounts a build normally creates. A number above the expected baseline is standing privilege nobody asked for.

items.name: AirDrop Disabled
items.description: Console sensor name: airdrop_disabled. True when AirDrop is blocked at machine scope. A common data-movement control, and one that a user cannot see is missing until they successfully send a file off the device.

items.name: APFS Local Snapshot Count
items.description: Console sensor name: local_snapshot_count. Number of local Time Machine snapshots on the boot volume. Snapshots are the usual explanation for a disk that reports far less free space than the file sizes account for.

items.name: App Store Application Count
items.description: Console sensor name: app_store_applications_count. Number of installed applications that carry a Mac App Store receipt. These update outside the managed patching path, which matters when you are trying to account for every version on the device.

items.name: Application Crash Reports In 30 Days
items.description: Console sensor name: crash_reports_30d. Count of user-space crash reports written in the last 30 days. A high number on one device points at hardware or a bad extension; the same number across a model points at a build.

items.name: Application Firewall Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: application_firewall_enabled. True when the macOS application firewall is on for either specific services or all incoming connections. Reads the global state directly rather than the UI, so it is accurate on a device with no console user.

items.name: Automated Device Enrollment
items.description: Console sensor name: dep_enrolled. True when the device is enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment rather than manually. Determines whether a wipe returns the device to management or to a personal setup assistant.

items.name: Automatic App Store Updates Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: automatic_app_updates_enabled. True when the App Store installs application updates automatically. Reported separately from system updates because the two settings drift apart and only one of them is usually in a profile.

items.name: Automatic Login Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: automatic_login_enabled. True when a user account logs in automatically at boot. Automatic login defeats FileVault at rest, because the device unlocks and signs in without anyone present.

items.name: Automatic Security Updates Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: automatic_security_updates_enabled. True when background installation of system data files and security responses is enabled. This is the setting that delivers XProtect and Rapid Security Response without a full OS update.

items.name: Battery Charging
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_charging. True while the battery is actively charging. Combined with the AC power sensor it separates a device on mains from one on mains with a dead charging circuit or a dock that is not delivering power.

items.name: Battery Condition
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_condition. Apple's own assessment: Normal, Replace Soon, Replace Now, Service Battery or Unknown. Unknown on a desktop with no battery, which is the expected answer there.

items.name: Battery Cycle Count
items.description: Charge cycles on the internal battery, or 0 on desktops. Supports battery replacement and hardware refresh planning.

items.name: Battery Maximum Capacity Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_maximum_capacity_percent. Current maximum charge capacity as a percentage of design capacity. Below roughly 80 percent the user is reporting a battery that will not last a meeting, and this is the number that justifies the replacement.

items.name: Bluetooth Radio Powered
items.description: Console sensor name: bluetooth_powered. True when the Bluetooth controller is on. Relevant both for peripherals that will not pair and for sites where the radio is meant to be off by policy.

items.name: Boot Volume Free Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: boot_volume_free_percent. Free space on the boot volume as a percentage. The percentage matters more than the absolute figure because macOS needs headroom for snapshots and updates in proportion to the disk.

items.name: Boot Volume Name
items.description: Console sensor name: boot_volume_name. The name of the volume the system booted from. A device booted from an external or a cloned volume shows up here, and that is worth knowing before chasing a policy that will not apply.

items.name: Boot Volume SMART Status
items.description: Console sensor name: boot_volume_smart_status. The drive's self-reported SMART state: Verified, Failing or Unknown. Anything other than Verified is a device to back up and replace rather than to troubleshoot.

items.name: Boot Volume Total GB
items.description: Console sensor name: boot_volume_total_gb. Total size of the boot volume in gigabytes. Pairs with the free-space sensors so a 3 percent warning on a 2 TB disk is not treated like one on a 128 GB disk.

items.name: Chrome Browser Version
items.description: Console sensor name: chrome_browser_version. Installed Google Chrome version, or NotInstalled. Browsers are the largest attack surface on a managed Mac and the one users update least reliably.

items.name: Computer Name
items.description: Console sensor name: computer_name. The friendly computer name as shown in Sharing. Drift between this, the local hostname and the asset record is the usual reason a device cannot be found by name during an incident.

items.name: Configuration Profile Count
items.description: Console sensor name: configuration_profile_count. Number of installed configuration profiles at device scope. A count of zero on an enrolled device, or a count far above the fleet norm, both point at a profile delivery problem.

items.name: Configured Printer Count
items.description: Console sensor name: printers_configured_count. Number of print queues configured on the device. Long-lived Macs accumulate queues for offices they no longer visit, and a broken default queue is a steady source of tickets.

items.name: Configured Time Zone
items.description: Console sensor name: timezone_configured. The device time zone. On a fleet where scripts and maintenance windows are scheduled locally, a wrong time zone quietly moves every scheduled action.

items.name: Content Caching Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: content_caching_enabled. True when the device is running the macOS content cache. Deliberate on a site server and usually accidental on a laptop, where it serves updates to strangers on the same network.

items.name: Custom Software Update Catalog Set
items.description: Console sensor name: software_update_catalog_url_set. True when a custom software update catalogue URL is configured. Almost always a leftover pointing at a retired internal update server, and it stops the device seeing Apple's updates entirely.

items.name: Custom Sudoers File Count
items.description: Console sensor name: custom_sudoers_files. Number of drop-in files under /etc/sudoers.d, excluding the shipped README. Each one can grant passwordless root to a user or a script, and they survive most reimaging shortcuts.

items.name: Days Since Last Reboot
items.description: Whole days since the last boot. Finds the Macs that never restart and so never finish pending updates.

items.name: Days Since Last Software Update Check
items.description: Console sensor name: days_since_last_software_update_check. Days since the software update mechanism last completed a successful check. A large number means the device is not talking to Apple's update service, which no patch policy can fix on its own.

items.name: Days Since Last Time Machine Backup
items.description: Console sensor name: time_machine_last_backup_days. Days since the newest Time Machine snapshot, derived from the backup path. Returns -1 where Time Machine is not configured or the destination is not attached, which is not the same as a failed backup.

items.name: Days To Nearest System Certificate Expiry
items.description: Console sensor name: system_certificate_min_days. Days until the soonest expiry among certificates in the System keychain. Negative means something has already expired; -1 means no certificate could be read at all.

items.name: Diagnostic Analytics Sharing Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: analytics_sharing_enabled. True when the device submits diagnostics and usage data to Apple. A privacy-posture setting most organisations decide once and then never verify on the devices that were built before the decision.

items.name: Downloads Folder Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: downloads_folder_size_gb. Combined size of every local user's Downloads folder in gigabytes. Usually the largest reclaimable area on a full laptop, and the one a user can clear themselves once they are shown the number.

items.name: Edge Browser Version
items.description: Console sensor name: edge_browser_version. Installed Microsoft Edge version, or NotInstalled. Worth tracking alongside Chrome on fleets where both are deployed and only one is being updated.

items.name: FileVault Deferred Enablement Pending
items.description: Console sensor name: filevault_deferred_enablement. True when FileVault is waiting for a user to sign in and finish enabling encryption. These devices report as targeted for encryption but are not actually encrypted, sometimes for months.

items.name: FileVault Enabled User Count
items.description: Console sensor name: filevault_enabled_user_count. Number of accounts that can unlock the FileVault volume at boot. Zero means only the recovery key can unlock it; a device where the primary user is not enabled will strand them after a restart.

items.name: FileVault Personal Recovery Key Present
items.description: Console sensor name: filevault_personal_recovery_key_present. True when a personal recovery key exists for FileVault. A device that is encrypted but has no escrowed key is one lost password away from unrecoverable data.

items.name: FileVault Status
items.description: Returns true when FileVault full-disk encryption is enabled.

items.name: Find My Mac Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: find_my_mac_enabled. True when Find My Mac is on. It is useful for a lost device and a problem for a returned one, because it can leave Activation Lock behind after the account is removed.

items.name: Firewall Stealth Mode Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: firewall_stealth_mode_enabled. True when the firewall does not answer ICMP or probes on closed ports. Stealth mode is the second half of the firewall baseline and is frequently missed because it is a separate checkbox.

items.name: Firmware Password Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: firmware_password_enabled. True when an Intel Mac has a firmware password set. Always false on Apple silicon, where the equivalent protection comes from the secure boot policy rather than a separate password.

items.name: Free Disk Space (GB)
items.description: Whole gigabytes available on the boot volume. Identifies Macs that will fail a macOS upgrade for lack of space.

items.name: Gatekeeper Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: gatekeeper_enabled. True when assessment of downloaded applications is enabled. Gatekeeper off means unsigned software runs without a prompt, and it is a common leftover from a developer or a troubleshooting session.

items.name: Guest Account Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: guest_account_enabled. True when the guest login is available at the login window. A guest session bypasses the audit trail that ties activity on the device to a person.

items.name: Hardware Model Identifier
items.description: Console sensor name: hardware_model_identifier. The model identifier, for example Mac15,7. More useful than a marketing name for working out which devices a macOS release will drop and which are due for replacement.

items.name: Homebrew Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: homebrew_installed. True when Homebrew is present. Not necessarily wrong, but it is an unmanaged package manager that installs software outside the patching pipeline, so the fleet should know where it is.

items.name: Hub Agent Running
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_service_running. True when a Workspace ONE Hub process is running. An enrolled device with the agent stopped stops reporting, but keeps its last known state in the console - which is why it looks fine.

items.name: Hub Agent Version
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_agent_version. Version of the Workspace ONE Intelligent Hub application. Returns NotInstalled where the app is absent, which is a different problem from an out-of-date agent.

items.name: Hub Full Disk Access Granted
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_full_disk_access_granted. True when a Workspace ONE component holds Full Disk Access in the privacy database. Without it, scripts running as root still cannot read Desktop, Documents or Downloads, which is why a working script returns nothing.

items.name: Hub Log Age Hours
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_log_age_hours. Hours since the Hub last wrote to its log, used as a proxy for the last check-in. A heuristic - a quiet agent and a stopped agent look similar - but it separates a device that is reporting from one that stopped days ago.

items.name: Installed Application Count
items.description: Console sensor name: applications_installed_count. Number of application bundles in /Applications. A useful shape measure for a fleet: devices far above the median are usually carrying software nobody has assessed.

items.name: Kernel Panics In 30 Days
items.description: Console sensor name: kernel_panics_30d. Count of panic reports written in the last 30 days. One is worth a look at the report; a pattern across a model or a driver version is a fleet problem rather than a device problem.

items.name: Local Hostname
items.description: Console sensor name: local_hostname. The Bonjour local hostname. It is set separately from the computer name and drifts on its own, which is why a device answers to one name on the network and another in the console.

items.name: Local User Account Count
items.description: Console sensor name: local_user_count. Number of local accounts with a UID of 500 or higher, which excludes the system and service accounts. Rising over time on a shared device usually means mobile accounts are never cleaned up.

items.name: macOS Version
items.description: Product version and build, for example '15.6 (24G84)'. Drives OS-version smart groups and upgrade reporting.

items.name: MDM Enrollment Status
items.description: Console sensor name: mdm_enrollment_status. Reports Enrolled, NotEnrolled or Unknown from the enrollment status rather than from the presence of an agent. A device with the Hub installed but no MDM enrolment cannot receive profiles or commands.

items.name: MDM Enrollment User Approved
items.description: Console sensor name: mdm_user_approved. True when the MDM enrolment is user approved or automated. Without approval a long list of management payloads silently do nothing, which is why a device can look enrolled and still ignore policy.

items.name: Memory Used Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: memory_used_percent. Percentage of physical memory that is not free, taken from the system memory pressure tool. A device sitting above 90 with heavy swap is a device that needs more memory, not a cleanup script.

items.name: Microsoft Office Version
items.description: Console sensor name: office_version. Version of Microsoft Word, used as the marker for the Office suite. Returns NotInstalled where Word is absent, which on most fleets means Office is absent.

items.name: Microsoft Teams Version
items.description: Console sensor name: teams_version. Version of the installed Teams client, checking the current app and the classic one. Old classic installs left beside the new client are a common source of duplicate notifications.

items.name: Mobile Accounts Present
items.description: Console sensor name: mobile_accounts_present. True when any local account is a cached directory account. Mobile accounts outlive the directory they came from, which is how a device ends up with a login nobody can disable centrally.

items.name: Network Time Server
items.description: Console sensor name: network_time_server. The configured time server. Devices still pointed at a decommissioned internal server look healthy until the clock drifts far enough to break authentication.

items.name: Network Time Sync Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: network_time_sync_enabled. True when the device sets its clock from a network time server. A drifted clock breaks Kerberos, certificate validation and MDM check-in, usually all at once.

items.name: OS Build Version
items.description: Console sensor name: os_build_version. The macOS build identifier, for example 24C101. The build is what distinguishes a device that took a Rapid Security Response from one that only looks the same by marketing version.

items.name: OS Major Version
items.description: Console sensor name: os_major_version. The major macOS version as an integer, for fleet segmentation and for finding the devices that a hardware cut-off has stranded on an older release.

items.name: Password Policy Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: password_policy_configured. True when a global account policy is present, meaning length, complexity or age rules are actually enforced locally rather than assumed from a profile that failed to install.

items.name: Pending Software Update Count
items.description: Console sensor name: pending_software_updates_count. Number of recommended updates the last software update check found, read from the cached result rather than by running a new scan. A device that never reaches zero is usually one that never finishes a restart.

items.name: Personal iCloud Account Signed In
items.description: Console sensor name: icloud_account_signed_in. True when any local user has an iCloud account configured. On a corporate fleet this is the sensor that finds devices syncing company documents into personal storage.

items.name: Physical Memory GB
items.description: Console sensor name: physical_memory_gb. Installed memory in whole gigabytes. On Apple silicon memory cannot be upgraded, so this is a replacement-planning figure as much as a diagnostic one.

items.name: Primary DNS Server
items.description: Console sensor name: primary_dns_server. The first resolver the system will ask. A public resolver here on a corporate device usually means split-brain internal names are about to fail.

items.name: Primary Network Interface
items.description: Console sensor name: primary_network_interface. The interface carrying the default route, for example en0. Tells you whether a device is on wireless, on a dock's ethernet or on a virtual adapter before you start reading its network complaints.

items.name: Processor Architecture
items.description: Console sensor name: processor_architecture. Reports arm64 or x86_64. The dividing line for Rosetta, for kernel extension support and for a good deal of software packaging, so it belongs in the inventory.

items.name: Processor Load Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: processor_load_percent. One-minute load average expressed as a percentage of available cores, so 100 means the machine is exactly saturated. More stable than an instantaneous CPU reading taken by a sensor that runs for a second.

items.name: Proxy Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: proxy_configured. True when an HTTP, HTTPS or automatic proxy configuration is active on the primary service. A stale proxy is a frequent cause of a device that is online but cannot reach management services.

items.name: Remote Login SSH Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: remote_login_enabled. True when SSH remote login is accepting connections. Inbound SSH on a laptop fleet is nearly always unintended and is a straightforward lateral movement path.

items.name: Remote Management Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: remote_management_enabled. True when the Apple Remote Desktop agent is running. Legitimate in some support models, but on most fleets it is an unmanaged remote control path that nobody remembers enabling.

items.name: Root Account Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: root_account_enabled. True when the root account has a password set and can be used to log in. Almost always a leftover from a support session and almost never intended on a managed endpoint.

items.name: Rosetta Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: rosetta_installed. True on Apple silicon when Rosetta 2 is present. Always false on Intel, where it is not applicable. Intel-only line-of-business software will not launch without it.

items.name: Safari Version
items.description: Console sensor name: safari_version. Installed Safari version. It ships with the OS but updates separately through software update, so a lagging Safari is a signal that updates are not being applied.

items.name: Screen Lock Grace Period Seconds
items.description: Console sensor name: screen_lock_grace_seconds. The longest grace period, in seconds, any local user has between the screen saver starting and a password being demanded. Returns -1 when no user preference exists to read.

items.name: Screen Lock Requires Password
items.description: Console sensor name: screen_lock_password_required. True when every local user profile requires a password to wake the screen saver. Checks each user's preference file rather than the current console user, so it is meaningful on a shared device.

items.name: Screen Sharing Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: screen_sharing_enabled. True when the built-in screen sharing service is loaded. Distinct from Remote Management, which the Apple Remote Desktop agent provides - both are reported separately.

items.name: Secure Boot Level
items.description: Console sensor name: secure_boot_level. Reports the boot security level as Full, Medium, Permissive or Unknown. Reads the iBridge or boot policy information; Unknown on older Intel hardware without a T2, which is itself worth knowing.

items.name: Secure Token Holder Count
items.description: Console sensor name: secure_token_holder_count. Number of local accounts holding a secure token. Zero on an encrypted device means no account can enable FileVault for anyone else, which is the state that turns a simple password reset into a rebuild.

items.name: Spotlight Indexing Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: spotlight_indexing_enabled. True when the boot volume is indexed. Indexing off breaks Spotlight search, Mail search and several management tools that rely on metadata queries, and users report it as 'search is broken'.

items.name: SSH Authorized Key Count
items.description: Console sensor name: ssh_authorized_keys_count. Total authorised public keys across all local home directories and the root account. A non-zero count on a laptop fleet is standing remote access that no directory group controls.

items.name: Swap Used MB
items.description: Console sensor name: swap_used_mb. Megabytes of swap currently in use. Sustained swap on an Apple silicon device with soldered memory is the clearest signal that the specification no longer matches the workload.

items.name: System Integrity Protection Enabled
items.description: Returns true when SIP is enabled. Flags Macs left with SIP disabled after imaging or troubleshooting.

items.name: System Log Directory Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: system_log_size_gb. Size of /private/var/log in gigabytes. A log directory measured in gigabytes usually means one component is failing in a loop and writing about it thousands of times a minute.

items.name: Thermal Throttling Active
items.description: Console sensor name: thermal_throttling_active. True when the scheduler or CPU speed limit is below 100, meaning the device is being held back by heat or power. The usual cause of 'my Mac got slow' on a device in a closed case or a dock in a warm room.

items.name: Third Party Kernel Extension Count
items.description: Console sensor name: third_party_kernel_extensions. Number of loaded kernel extensions that are not Apple's. Each one is a candidate cause for a panic and a blocker for future macOS releases, so a fleet that is trying to get to zero needs to be able to count them.

items.name: Third Party Launch Agent Count
items.description: Console sensor name: third_party_launch_agents. Number of non-Apple launch agents installed at machine scope. Each one starts code in every user session, so an unexplained rise is worth investigating rather than tidying away.

items.name: Third Party Launch Daemon Count
items.description: Console sensor name: third_party_launch_daemons. Number of non-Apple launch daemons. These run as root at boot with no user present, so this is the more important half of the persistence pair.

items.name: Time Machine Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: time_machine_configured. True when automatic Time Machine backups are enabled. On a fleet that relies on cloud sync this should be uniformly false; a scattering of true is usually a user's personal disk.

items.name: Touch ID For Sudo Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: sudo_touchid_enabled. True when the PAM stack allows Touch ID to authorise sudo. A small convenience that reduces password entry in shared spaces, and one that upgrades used to silently remove until the sudo_local file existed.

items.name: Trash Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: trash_size_gb. Combined size of every local user's Trash in gigabytes. Space the device has already given up on but has not released, and the cheapest thing to reclaim on a disk-full ticket.

items.name: User Cache Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: user_caches_size_gb. Combined size of every local user's Library Caches folder in gigabytes. The first place to look when a disk is full and no obvious large file explains it.

items.name: VPN Configuration Count
items.description: Console sensor name: vpn_configuration_count. Number of network extension VPN configurations present. Zero on a fleet that is meant to have a client, or several on a device that should have one, are both worth chasing.

items.name: Wireless Network SSID
items.description: Console sensor name: wifi_ssid. The SSID the device is joined to, or None when it is not on wireless. Useful for spotting devices sitting on a guest or personal network while inside the office.

items.name: Wireless Signal RSSI
items.description: Console sensor name: wifi_signal_rssi. Received signal strength in dBm as a negative integer, for example -58. Returns 0 when the device is not on wireless. Anything past -70 explains a slow session better than a bandwidth test will.

items.name: Xcode Command Line Tools Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: xcode_command_line_tools_installed. True when the command line developer tools are present. Expected on engineering devices and worth a question elsewhere, since they bring a compiler and git onto a standard build.

items.name: XProtect Definition Version
items.description: Console sensor name: xprotect_version. The XProtect malware definition bundle version. Compare across the fleet: a device several versions behind is not receiving background content updates, whatever its OS patch level says.

items.name: XProtect Remediator Version
items.description: Console sensor name: xprotect_remediator_version. Version of the XProtect Remediator app, the component that actually removes known malware families. It updates separately from the definition bundle, so both are worth reporting.

items.name: Zoom Version
items.description: Console sensor name: zoom_version. Installed Zoom client version, or NotInstalled. Zoom self-updates by default, so a device several versions behind usually has the update path blocked rather than the app abandoned.

items.name: Accounts With An Empty Password
items.description: Console sensor name: empty_password_accounts. Number of accounts in the shadow file whose password field is empty. Any result above zero is an unauthenticated login waiting to happen and should be treated as an incident.

items.name: Address Space Randomisation Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: address_space_randomisation_enabled. True when kernel.randomize_va_space is set to full randomisation. Turned down on some legacy application hosts and then never turned back up after the application was retired.

items.name: Audit Daemon Running
items.description: Console sensor name: auditd_running. True when auditd is active. Without it the kernel's audit events go nowhere, and an investigation into what happened on the device has almost nothing to read.

items.name: Automatic Reboot After Update Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: automatic_reboot_configured. True when the automatic update mechanism is allowed to restart the device on its own. Worth knowing before an unplanned reboot during business hours is blamed on something else.

items.name: Battery Present
items.description: Console sensor name: battery_present. True when the device has a battery, which separates the laptops from the desktops and virtual machines in a mixed fleet without relying on the naming convention.

items.name: Blacklisted Kernel Module Count
items.description: Console sensor name: kernel_module_blacklist_count. Number of modules explicitly blacklisted in modprobe configuration. The measure of how much of a module-hardening baseline has actually landed on this device.

items.name: Broken Package Count
items.description: Console sensor name: broken_packages_count. Number of packages in a half-configured or half-installed state. A non-zero count blocks every future install and is usually the reason a deployment silently stops working on one device.

items.name: Configured Time Zone
items.description: Console sensor name: timezone. The device time zone. On a fleet where maintenance windows and cron jobs are scheduled locally, a wrong time zone silently moves every scheduled action.

items.name: Container Runtime
items.description: Console sensor name: container_runtime. Which container runtime is installed: docker, podman, containerd or None. Determines whether the workload sensors on this host mean anything and whether image patching is in scope.

items.name: Core Dumps Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: core_dumps_enabled. True when a process is allowed to write a core dump. Cores can contain secrets held in memory, so most hardened baselines set the limit to zero and most default installs do not.

items.name: CPU Core Count
items.description: Console sensor name: cpu_core_count. Number of online logical processors. Segments a fleet, sizes a workload and gives every load-average threshold something to be relative to.

items.name: CPU Model Name
items.description: Console sensor name: cpu_model_name. The processor model string. Useful for finding the devices affected by a microcode advisory and for spotting hardware that is out of its support window.

items.name: CPU Temperature Celsius
items.description: Console sensor name: cpu_temperature_celsius. Highest thermal zone reading in whole degrees. Returns -1 on hardware that exposes no thermal zone, which includes most virtual machines.

items.name: Days Since Last Interactive Login
items.description: Console sensor name: days_since_last_login. Days since any real user last logged in. A high number on a workstation means the device is idle or abandoned; on a server it is entirely normal and confirms nobody is hand-managing it.

items.name: Days Since Last Package Update
items.description: Console sensor name: days_since_last_package_update. Days since the package database last recorded an install or upgrade. A large number is the clearest sign that a device has fallen out of the patching pipeline entirely.

items.name: Days Since Last Reboot
items.description: Whole days of uptime from /proc/uptime. Finds hosts still running a kernel that a patch cycle has already replaced.

items.name: Default Gateway Present
items.description: Console sensor name: default_gateway_present. True when the device has a default route. False on a host that is up and reachable on its own segment but cannot reach anything beyond it, which is a very specific and common fault.

items.name: Desktop Environment
items.description: Console sensor name: desktop_environment. The installed desktop session type - GNOME, KDE, XFCE or Headless. Separates the workstation fleet from the server fleet without relying on a naming convention.

items.name: Disk SMART Health
items.description: Console sensor name: disk_smart_health. Reports PASSED, FAILED or Unavailable for the first physical disk. Unavailable is the honest answer on a virtual machine or where smartmontools is not installed.

items.name: Display Manager Automatic Login
items.description: Console sensor name: display_manager_autologin. True when the graphical login manager is configured to sign a user in without a password. Defeats disk encryption at rest and is usually left behind from a kiosk or lab build.

items.name: Distribution Name
items.description: The PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release, for example 'Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS'. Groups a mixed Linux estate by distribution and release.

items.name: DKMS Modules Not Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: dkms_modules_not_installed. Number of DKMS modules that are registered but not built for the running kernel. This is why a graphics or VPN driver stops working after a kernel update and only after the reboot.

items.name: Encrypted Volume Entry Count
items.description: Console sensor name: crypttab_entry_count. Number of entries in /etc/crypttab, meaning volumes that are unlocked at boot from a key or a passphrase. Read alongside the root volume encryption sensor to see the whole picture.

items.name: Endpoint Security Agent Present
items.description: Console sensor name: endpoint_security_agent_present. True when a recognised endpoint security agent process is running - Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Carbon Black or ClamAV. Detects the process, not the package, so a stopped agent reads as absent.

items.name: Fail2ban Running
items.description: Console sensor name: fail2ban_running. True when fail2ban is active. On an internet-facing host it is the difference between a brute force attempt being slowed and being allowed to run all night.

items.name: Failed Systemd Unit Count
items.description: Console sensor name: failed_systemd_units. Number of systemd units in the failed state. Returns -1 where systemd is not the init system. The single most informative health number on a modern Linux host.

items.name: File Descriptor Usage Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: file_descriptor_usage_percent. System-wide open file descriptors as a percentage of the kernel maximum. A host approaching the limit starts refusing connections in ways that look like a network fault.

items.name: Firewall Active
items.description: Console sensor name: firewall_active. True when nftables, iptables or a front end such as ufw or firewalld is actually filtering. Checks for rules rather than for an installed package, because an installed firewall with no rules filters nothing.

items.name: Firewall Default Input Policy
items.description: Console sensor name: firewall_default_input_policy. The default policy for inbound traffic: DROP, REJECT, ACCEPT or Unknown. A firewall with rules but an ACCEPT default only blocks what someone remembered to name.

items.name: Flatpak Package Count
items.description: Console sensor name: flatpak_packages_count. Number of installed flatpaks. Like snaps, they sit outside the package manager's view, which matters when you are trying to account for every version of an application on the fleet.

items.name: Free Disk Space (GB)
items.description: Whole gigabytes available on the root filesystem. Drives the low-disk smart group used before package upgrades.

items.name: Fullest Mount Usage Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: fullest_mount_usage_percent. The highest usage percentage across all local filesystems. Catches a full /var or /home on a device whose root filesystem still looks perfectly healthy.

items.name: Hardware Vendor And Model
items.description: Console sensor name: hardware_vendor_model. The system vendor and product name from DMI, for example 'Dell Inc. Latitude 7440'. Returns the hypervisor product string on a virtual machine, which is itself useful.

items.name: Hostname
items.description: Console sensor name: hostname. The device's configured hostname. Drift between this and the asset record is the usual reason a host cannot be found by name in the middle of an incident.

items.name: Hub Agent Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_agent_installed. True when the Workspace ONE Intelligent Hub for Linux is installed. The first thing to establish before anything else about management state means much.

items.name: Hub Agent Version
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_agent_version. Version of the installed Hub agent, or NotInstalled. An out-of-date agent and a missing agent are different problems and are worth telling apart in one column.

items.name: Hub Log Age Hours
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_log_age_hours. Hours since the Hub last wrote to its log, used as a proxy for the last check-in. A heuristic - a quiet agent and a stopped agent look alike - but it separates a reporting device from one that stopped days ago.

items.name: Hub Service Active
items.description: Console sensor name: hub_service_active. True when the Hub's systemd service is running. An enrolled device with a stopped agent keeps its last reported state in the console, which is why it still looks healthy.

items.name: ICMP Redirects Accepted
items.description: Console sensor name: icmp_redirects_accepted. True when the kernel will accept an ICMP redirect and change its routing table. An old default that lets anyone on the local segment steer this device's traffic.

items.name: Inactive User Account Count
items.description: Console sensor name: inactive_user_accounts. Number of interactive accounts that have never logged in or have not logged in for more than 90 days. The leaver list, derived from the device rather than from the directory.

items.name: Init System
items.description: Console sensor name: init_system. Whether PID 1 is systemd, sysvinit, openrc or something else. Every service-related script has to branch on this, so it belongs in the inventory rather than in each script's guesswork.

items.name: Installed Package Count
items.description: Console sensor name: installed_package_count. Total packages installed. A shape measure rather than a threshold: devices far from the fleet median are usually carrying software that was never part of the build.

items.name: IP Forwarding Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: ip_forwarding_enabled. True when the kernel is routing packets between interfaces. Expected on a gateway or a container host and a finding anywhere else, because it turns an endpoint into a path between networks.

items.name: Kernel Livepatch Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: livepatch_enabled. True when a kernel live patching service is active. On fleets that cannot take a reboot window this is the control that keeps kernel vulnerabilities closed between restarts.

items.name: Kernel Lockdown Mode
items.description: Console sensor name: kernel_lockdown_mode. Reports none, integrity or confidentiality. Lockdown restricts what even root can do to the running kernel, and it is one of the few controls that survives a root compromise.

items.name: Kernel Taint Value
items.description: Console sensor name: kernel_taint_value. The kernel taint bitmask. Anything other than zero means an out-of-tree module, a firmware warning or a prior oops, and it changes how much a vendor will help with a crash.

items.name: Listening TCP Port Count
items.description: Console sensor name: listening_tcp_port_count. Number of distinct TCP ports in the listening state. The size of the network attack surface in one number, and a useful thing to watch for change rather than for an absolute value.

items.name: Load Average Per Core Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: load_average_per_core_percent. The one-minute load average as a percentage of available cores, so 100 means exactly saturated. More stable than an instantaneous CPU reading taken during a one-second sensor run.

items.name: Local User Account Count
items.description: Console sensor name: local_user_count. Number of accounts with a UID of 1000 or higher and a real login shell, which excludes the service accounts. Growth over time on a server usually means leavers were never removed.

items.name: Log Directory Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: var_log_size_gb. Size of /var/log in gigabytes. A log directory measured in gigabytes usually means one component is failing in a loop and writing about it thousands of times a minute.

items.name: Logged In User Count
items.description: Console sensor name: logged_in_user_count. Number of distinct users with an active session. Useful before a maintenance action, and useful afterwards when someone asks who was on the host at the time.

items.name: Mandatory Access Control Status
items.description: Console sensor name: mandatory_access_control_status. Reports SELinux-Enforcing, SELinux-Permissive, SELinux-Disabled, AppArmor-Enabled or None. Permissive is the state worth finding: it looks configured in an audit and enforces nothing.

items.name: Memory Used Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: memory_used_percent. Percentage of physical memory in use, calculated from MemAvailable so cache and buffers are not counted as used. The figure that matches what the kernel would actually give a new process.

items.name: Network Configuration Manager
items.description: Console sensor name: network_configuration_manager. Which stack owns the network configuration: NetworkManager, systemd-networkd, ifupdown or netplan. Every network change script has to branch on this before it edits anything.

items.name: OS Family
items.description: Console sensor name: os_id_like. The ID_LIKE value from /etc/os-release, falling back to ID. Tells a script whether it is on a Debian, RHEL or SUSE derivative before it picks a package manager.

items.name: OS Version ID
items.description: Console sensor name: os_version_id. The VERSION_ID from /etc/os-release, for example 22.04 or 9.4. Read from the file rather than a command, so it works identically on every distribution family.

items.name: Out Of Memory Kills In 7 Days
items.description: Console sensor name: oom_kills_7d. Number of times the kernel killed a process to reclaim memory in the last week. A single event explains a service that vanished without a crash report.

items.name: Package Manager
items.description: Console sensor name: package_manager. Which package manager the device actually has: apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman or None. Detected rather than assumed, so a script can branch on it instead of guessing from the distribution name.

items.name: Package Manager Lock Held
items.description: Console sensor name: package_manager_lock_held. True when another process is holding the package database lock right now. Reported rather than acted on - a sensor must never wait for a lock, and never remove one.

items.name: Password Maximum Age Days
items.description: Console sensor name: password_max_age_days. The PASS_MAX_DAYS value from login.defs, which sets how long a new account's password may live. Returns -1 where the file cannot be read; 99999 is the default that means never.

items.name: Passwordless Sudo Entry Count
items.description: Console sensor name: sudo_nopasswd_entries. Number of NOPASSWD rules in the sudoers file and its drop-in directory. Each one turns a compromised user session straight into root without a prompt.

items.name: Pending Package Updates
items.description: Counts packages with available updates across apt, dnf/yum and zypper hosts.

items.name: Physical Memory GB
items.description: Console sensor name: physical_memory_gb. Installed memory in whole gigabytes. Basic inventory, and the denominator for every memory threshold worth setting.

items.name: Ports Listening On All Interfaces
items.description: Console sensor name: listening_on_all_interfaces_count. Number of TCP ports bound to 0.0.0.0 or the IPv6 wildcard rather than to loopback. These are the ports actually reachable from the network, which is the number that matters.

items.name: Primary DNS Server
items.description: Console sensor name: primary_dns_server. The first resolver the device will ask, read from systemd-resolved where it is in use and from resolv.conf otherwise. A public resolver on a corporate host means internal names are about to fail.

items.name: Primary IP Address
items.description: Console sensor name: primary_ip_address. The source address the device would use to reach the internet, taken from the routing table rather than from an interface list, so it is the address that actually matters.

items.name: Processor Architecture
items.description: Console sensor name: architecture. The machine architecture, for example x86_64 or aarch64. Determines which packages and agent builds apply, and it is the first thing a mixed fleet needs to segment on.

items.name: Proxy Environment Configured
items.description: Console sensor name: proxy_environment_configured. True when a proxy is set in the system-wide environment or in the package manager's own configuration. A stale proxy here is a common reason updates fail on one host and nowhere else.

items.name: RAID Array Degraded
items.description: Console sensor name: raid_array_degraded. True when a software RAID array is running with a missing or failed member. Returns false where no software RAID is configured, which is the common case on an endpoint.

items.name: Read Only Mount Count
items.description: Console sensor name: read_only_mount_count. Number of local filesystems mounted read-only that are not meant to be. A filesystem the kernel has remounted read-only after an error is a device about to fail in a confusing way.

items.name: Reboot Required
items.description: Returns true when the package manager or a kernel update is waiting on a restart, across apt, dnf/yum and zypper hosts.

items.name: Repository Signature Check Disabled
items.description: Console sensor name: repository_signature_check_disabled. True when any repository is configured to skip GPG verification. A single gpgcheck=0 turns the whole update path into an unauthenticated one, and it is usually a leftover from a hurried install.

items.name: Resolver Configuration Manager
items.description: Console sensor name: resolv_conf_manager. Which component owns /etc/resolv.conf: systemd-resolved, NetworkManager, resolvconf or static. Editing the file by hand on a managed host is why a DNS change keeps reverting.

items.name: Root Filesystem Free Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: root_filesystem_free_percent. Free space on the root filesystem as a percentage. The percentage travels better across a mixed fleet than an absolute figure, and it is what a threshold should be written against.

items.name: Root Filesystem Inode Usage Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: inode_usage_percent. Percentage of inodes used on the root filesystem. A device can be out of inodes with gigabytes free, and the error it produces looks exactly like a full disk.

items.name: Root Filesystem Total GB
items.description: Console sensor name: root_filesystem_total_gb. Total size of the root filesystem in gigabytes. Pairs with the free-percent sensor so a 5 percent warning on a 2 TB volume is not treated like one on a 20 GB volume.

items.name: Root Volume Encrypted
items.description: Returns true when the root filesystem sits on a LUKS or dm-crypt device. Provides the encryption-at-rest datapoint for Linux compliance reporting.

items.name: Running Container Count
items.description: Console sensor name: running_container_count. Number of containers currently running. Returns -1 where no runtime is installed or the daemon cannot be queried without extra privilege.

items.name: Running Kernel Is The Newest Installed
items.description: Console sensor name: running_kernel_is_newest. True when the running kernel matches the newest kernel on disk. False is the honest way to report 'patched but not restarted', which a package count alone will not tell you.

items.name: Running Kernel Version
items.description: Console sensor name: kernel_version. The kernel release currently running. Compared against the newest installed kernel it shows a device that has been patched but never restarted.

items.name: Secure Boot Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: secure_boot_enabled. True when UEFI Secure Boot is active. False on a BIOS system as well as on a UEFI system with it turned off, so read it alongside the firmware mode rather than on its own.

items.name: Security Updates Pending
items.description: Console sensor name: security_updates_pending. Number of pending updates the package manager marks as security, read from the cached metadata without taking a lock. Returns -1 where the family does not separate security updates.

items.name: Snap Package Count
