items.description: Console sensor name: snap_packages_count. Number of installed snaps. Snaps update themselves on their own schedule, outside the package manager, so they are worth counting separately from everything else on the device.

items.name: SSH Authorized Key Count
items.description: Console sensor name: ssh_authorized_keys_count. Total authorised public keys across every home directory and root. Standing remote access that no directory group governs, and the count usually only ever goes up.

items.name: SSH Password Authentication Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: ssh_password_authentication_enabled. True when sshd will accept a password. Reads the effective configuration including drop-in files, because the setting is very often overridden in a file nobody remembers adding.

items.name: SSH Root Login Permitted
items.description: Console sensor name: ssh_root_login_permitted. True when root may log in over SSH by any method. prohibit-password still counts as permitted here, because a key-based root login is still a root login without an audit trail.

items.name: SSH Service Running
items.description: Console sensor name: ssh_service_running. True when an SSH daemon is listening. Expected on a server fleet and worth questioning on a desktop one, so read it against what the device is supposed to be.

items.name: Sudo Group Member Count
items.description: Console sensor name: sudo_group_member_count. Number of accounts in the sudo or wheel group. The practical measure of how many people can become root on this device, which is rarely the number anyone expects.

items.name: SUID Binary Count
items.description: Console sensor name: suid_binary_count. Number of set-uid binaries in the standard binary directories. The absolute number matters less than the change: a device that gains one has gained a new route to root.

items.name: Swap Total MB
items.description: Console sensor name: swap_total_mb. Total configured swap in megabytes. Zero on a host that was built without swap, which is a deliberate choice in some container fleets and an oversight in others.

items.name: Swap Used Percent
items.description: Console sensor name: swap_used_percent. Percentage of configured swap in use. Returns -1 where there is no swap. Sustained swap use is the clearest sign that the memory allocation no longer matches the workload.

items.name: Systemd Journal Size MB
items.description: Console sensor name: journal_size_mb. Size of the systemd journal in megabytes. Returns -1 where journald is not in use. An unbounded journal is one of the most common causes of a slowly filling root volume.

items.name: Systemd State Degraded
items.description: Console sensor name: systemd_state_degraded. True when systemd reports the overall system state as degraded, meaning at least one unit failed to start. A single boolean that covers the whole service estate on the device.

items.name: Systemd Timer Count
items.description: Console sensor name: systemd_timer_count. Number of enabled systemd timers. The modern replacement for cron, and where scheduled work actually lives on a current distribution.

items.name: Temp Directory Size GB
items.description: Console sensor name: tmp_size_gb. Combined size of /tmp and /var/tmp in gigabytes. On a host where /tmp is not a tmpfs this grows without limit, and it is usually one application leaving files behind.

items.name: Third Party Repository Count
items.description: Console sensor name: third_party_repositories_count. Number of configured software repositories that are not the distribution's own. Each one is an unreviewed source of root-level code and a candidate cause when one device has a package nobody else does.

items.name: Time Synchronisation Active
items.description: Console sensor name: time_sync_active. True when chrony, systemd-timesyncd or ntpd is running and synchronised. A drifted clock breaks Kerberos, TLS validation and log correlation at the same time.

items.name: Time Synchronisation Daemon
items.description: Console sensor name: time_sync_daemon. Which time daemon is in use: chrony, systemd-timesyncd, ntpd or None. Two of them installed at once is a classic cause of a clock that will not settle.

items.name: TPM Device Present
items.description: Console sensor name: tpm_device_present. True when a TPM device node exists. Determines whether disk encryption can be sealed to the platform rather than depending on a passphrase somebody has to type or store.

items.name: UID Zero Account Count
items.description: Console sensor name: uid_zero_account_count. Number of accounts with UID 0. Anything above one is a second root by another name, and it is a classic persistence mechanism as well as a classic misconfiguration.

items.name: Unattended Upgrades Enabled
items.description: Console sensor name: unattended_upgrades_enabled. True when the distribution's automatic update mechanism is enabled - unattended-upgrades, dnf-automatic or the zypper timer. The single most useful patching sensor on a fleet nobody logs into.

items.name: USB Storage Module Loaded
items.description: Console sensor name: usb_storage_module_loaded. True when the usb-storage kernel module is loaded, meaning removable drives will mount. The practical measure of a removable media restriction on Linux, where there is no single switch for it.

items.name: User Cron Job Count
items.description: Console sensor name: user_cron_job_count. Number of user crontabs installed. User cron is a persistence mechanism nobody audits and a scheduling mechanism nobody documents, so the count is worth watching for change.

items.name: Virtualization Platform
items.description: Console sensor name: virtualization_platform. Reports the hypervisor or container runtime the device is running under, or 'none' on bare metal. Determines which hardware sensors mean anything on this device.

items.name: World Writable Directories Without Sticky Bit
items.description: Console sensor name: world_writable_without_sticky. Number of world-writable directories under /var and /opt that do not carry the sticky bit, so any user can delete another's files there. Bounded to those two trees to keep the sensor cheap.

items.name: Zombie Process Count
items.description: Console sensor name: zombie_process_count. Number of processes in the zombie state. A handful is noise; a steadily rising count means a parent process is not reaping its children and will eventually exhaust the process table.
